The same reverse dependency also sits in `escalation/merge_lane_resolution.py` (2 function-local imports of orchestrator.merge_queue) and `escalation/git_authority.py` (2, orchestrator.landing_evidence). That makes 14 function-local escalation→orchestrator imports, so escalation is not a lower layer (heuristic 9). Partitions (a)–(e) split legitimately. (f) and (g), 1,559 lines or 39% of create_server, cannot be made heuristic-13-clean anywhere inside the escalation package, because they are orchestrator code hosted on escalation's FastMCP instance. Because of the closure shape, every tool's only anchor is `create_server`, and tests reach behaviour through `(await server.get_tool(n)).fn`. Fix-history: 142 commits touched this file since 2026-07-01, 56 of them matching 'fix'.
findings.proposal: Split along partitions (a)–(e) into escalation modules that register tools onto a passed FastMCP instance, with the closure state (_promote_lock, the storm counter, the injected lookups) carried as one explicit context object. Move (f)+(g) into the orchestrator, for example an orchestrator/mcp module that registers merge/scheduler/worktree tools onto the server the harness creates. That removes all 14 reverse imports and both re-export-shim dependencies. Re-home the reviewer-answering prose in the tool docstrings into commits or task records, and keep the agent-facing contract text. This is a design choice about which package owns the merge-tool surface.

findings.statement: Heuristic 9 (layering): orchestrator depends on escalation at runtime, yet escalation's src reaches back up into orchestrator internals through function-local imports — server.py imports `orchestrator.merge_queue` (the sys.modules alias shim for merge_lane.worker) at four sites, `orchestrator.merge_lane`, `orchestrator.landing_evidence` (another alias shim), `orchestrator.event_store`, `orchestrator.git_ops.InteractiveWorktreeLimitError` (inside `claim_warm_worktree`) and the PRIVATE `orchestrator.git_ops._run` (inside `release_warm_worktree`, commented 'Runtime-only reverse import'); merge_lane_resolution.py imports `orchestrator.merge_queue` twice and git_authority.py `orchestrator.landing_evidence` twice. Every one carries `# type: ignore[reportMissingImports]`, so escalation's pyright gate cannot see those call sites, and escalation/pyproject.toml declares orchestrator only as a dev dependency with a comment saying it is 'Dev-only — does not affect the published escalation package', which the runtime imports contradict. These are heuristic 13's symptoms (function-local imports placed to break a cycle; reliance on re-export shims) and a heuristic 7 reach into another package's private name. The next change to the merge lane's module layout (the planned retirement of the 14 alias shims) breaks the escalation server at runtime with no type-check or import-time signal — the dead-code seat measured `orchestrator.merge_queue` as still imported by escalation src.
findings.proposal: Choose a layering: either move the pure pieces escalation needs (MERGE_LANES, landing-evidence readers, a worktree-remove helper) into a lower layer both import (shared), or invert the dependency with a port escalation defines and orchestrator injects at server construction. Either choice also fixes the false dev-only comment and removes the type-ignores. Chooses between designs.

findings.statement: This is heuristic 12, 'status strings that are really enums', together with heuristic 11 and INV-1. Escalation `category` drives routing: `_chokepoint_or_submit`'s review_suggestions bypass, `DedupeConfig.infra_dedupe_categories`, `authority.L2_AUTO_CLOSE_DENY_CATEGORIES`, `shadow_ruling.GATED_CATEGORIES`/`_MILESTONE_CATEGORIES`, `_MARKUP_STORM_CATEGORY`'s own dedup, and 32 `category ==/in` tests across first-party source. Yet the vocabulary is an inert 15-item list (`server.py::CATEGORIES`). action_effects.py and provenance_conflict.py both call it 'inert/unvalidated', and the escalate_* tools never check it. A `category='…'` grep finds more than 40 distinct literal spellings in source (wip_conflict, preexisting_main_break, verify_host_unreachable, merge_request_stuck, …), most absent from the list. `models.py::Escalation.category`'s comment says 'REFACTOR TRIGGER (task 3709) … The NEXT category addition promotes this comment to an enum', and categories have since been added (stranded_merge_failed to CATEGORIES with 'vocabulary parity only', mcp_markup_storm as a server constant) without the promotion. A typo'd category files cleanly and silently escapes every routing rule keyed on it.
findings.proposal: Promote category to a closed enum, or to a registry each producer declares into with a submit-time check, in models.py. Import it everywhere a category is routed on. Decide whether an unknown category is rejected or quarantined. This changes the filing contract for every producer.

findings.statement: Heuristic 7, prefer stateless interactions between modules. The briefing's known gap is verified as still present. The escalation MCP server receives the whole Harness typed as Any and reads its private state by duck typing: getattr(harness, '_merge_worker', None) in _get_merge_worker, used at four call sites, each followed by hasattr(worker, 'snapshot'), and getattr(harness, '_terminal_retention', None) in _get_terminal_retention, used at three. It also reaches harness.git_ops, harness.scheduler and harness.is_workflow_active. The snapshot crosses the boundary as a dict read by string keys (snap.get('entries'), snap.get('depth'), e.get('request_id')). The docstring states the fix ('a public harness.merge_worker_snapshot() accessor ... requires a harness module change scoped to a separate task'), but no such accessor exists on Harness (task_runtime_snapshot does). A rename of Harness._merge_worker degrades every merge_request, get_merge_queue and merge_status position read to 'Merge worker not available', silently and by design ('degrades gracefully rather than crashing').
findings.proposal: Define a narrow Protocol, for example OrchestratorPort, with merge_queue_snapshot() -> a typed MergeQueueSnapshot, terminal_retention() and the few other calls the server needs. Harness implements it and create_server takes it instead of Any. Delete the getattr probes. The change spans the escalation and orchestrator packages.

findings.statement: This violates INV-13 (readers-prove-their-producer). `merge_status` Tier 2 and `merge_cancel`'s waiter-absent branch read a TerminalOutcomeRetention ring through `_get_terminal_retention`, a getattr probe of the private `harness._terminal_retention`. No production code assigns that attribute (`git grep` over orchestrator/src finds no `_terminal_retention =`). The function's own docstring states that it 'always resolves to None outside tests', and merge_request passes the same None as its `retention=` write side. So a reader, a write call and two tiers of documented lookup order exist with no producer. Tier 3 (`event_store.latest_merge_finalized`) is run-scoped by default (`cross_run=False`). Tier 3.5 (git-authority) can only confirm landings. So after an orchestrator restart, a prior-run conflict/blocked/abandoned outcome is answered `state: 'unknown', hint: 'check git log main'`, and merge_cancel of a prior-run id is 'unknown'. That is the run-scoped-cache answer codebook entry merge-state-not-git-corroborated records (10 sightings). `_get_merge_worker`'s `getattr(harness, '_merge_worker')`, the briefing's known h7 gap, is the same duck-typed private reach, used by get_merge_queue, merge_request's position and merge_status Tier 1.
findings.proposal: Pick one of two: either mount the ring in the harness, or delete Tier 2 and the retention plumbing (task 3149 is cited in the docstring as owning this choice). Give the harness public accessors for the merge worker snapshot and halt state in place of private getattr probes. Have merge_status read the event store cross-run with the is_current_run label (plans/merge-status-durable-non-landed-prd.md, task 4831, per the in-code note).

findings.statement: This is an INV-5 (no-lockstep-duplication) copy that has already drifted (heuristic 11). When `merge_request(verified_green=True)` is called, it emits `EventType.workflow_verify` with data `{passed, base_sha, branch}`. Its 'SYNC CONTRACT' comment says the payload 'MUST stay byte-identical to the orchestrator's own emission at workflow.py:1724-1733' and records that the shared constructor was deferred. The orchestrator's emission (`workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._enter_phase`) now also writes `tip_sha` (task 2752), and two readers key on it: `orchestrator/verify_checkpoint.py::green_checkpoint_at_tip` requires `data['tip_sha'] == tip_sha`, and `stranded_verified_green.py::last_verified_green_tip` ignores passed rows without a tip. The server path has `resolved_tip` in hand and omits it. So a human- or /merge-queue-vouched green is invisible to the verify checkpoint and to the stranded-verified-green remediation, while still counting for the `passed`-only readers. The two copies now disagree, and no test notices.
findings.proposal: Extract one `emit_workflow_verify(event_store, task_id, *, tip_sha, base_sha, branch)` in the orchestrator and call it from both sites. The minimal stop-gap is to add `tip_sha: resolved_tip` to the server payload. The real fix spans two packages.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10: the write-time identity invariant is an unchecked precondition. GraphitiBackend.ensure_entity_node and GraphitiBackend._resolve_or_create_entity document that callers 'MUST hold _identity_lock_for(group_id)' (3× in graphiti_client.py, 3× in memory_service.py) but neither checks it — no `.locked()` anywhere in graphiti_client.py. Heuristic 7: the contract crosses the module boundary through private names — MemoryService calls self.graphiti._identity_lock_for (memory_service.py, 2 sites) and self.graphiti._resolve_or_create_entity; MemoryService._repair_episode_referents says the lock is held 'by PLACEMENT' and 'calling it from anywhere that does not already hold the lock would reintroduce the race'. A future caller that forgets the lock mints the duplicate-name node pair the identity gate exists to prevent, silently.
findings.proposal: Either make the lock part of the public interface (an identity_section(group_id) context manager; minting methods assert lock.locked() and raise a named violation carrying group_id) or have the backend acquire it itself and drop the precondition — a choice between designs.

findings.statement: INV-11 no-silent-fail-soft: get_statuses_fresh is documented and implemented to return `{}` 'if the DB file does not exist yet or the read fails for any reason'. Any exception, including one while opening the connection, is caught, logged at WARNING and returned as an empty census that cannot be told apart from a real empty one, and with ids= a failed read means 'every id unknown'. The protocol (task_backend_protocol.py) and TaskInterceptor.get_statuses_fresh forward this unchanged. Each consumer must re-invent failure detection. reconciliation/orphaned_recon_escalation_sweep.py does it twice ('treating as a FAILED read (get_statuses_fresh fails open to {} on any error)'), and its docstring warns that an errored read 'would render as missing for every record'. reconciliation/harness.py::_fetch_task_count_census 'degrade[s] to an empty dict'. The next consumer that does not know the empty-means-failed folklore will act on a phantom empty census: the destructive 'missing id = deleted' pattern get_statuses' own docstring describes for the lane-checkout reconciler.
findings.proposal: Make the shortfall part of the result: raise (and let callers decide), or return a typed census with `complete: bool` / an error field, and delete the per-consumer 'empty means failed' heuristics. Changes a protocol contract; structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12: ReconciliationConfig.agent_llm_provider and judge_llm_provider are bare `str` fields (default 'claude_cli'), unlike LLMConfig.provider/client_class/structured_output_mode in the same file, which are Literal-typed and validated. The provider axis is then dispatched by two independent if/elif chains that disagree on unknown values (h10 'uniformly'): agent_loop.py::AgentLoop._call_llm raises ValueError('Unsupported agent LLM provider'), while judge.py::Judge._call_llm sends every value that is not 'claude_cli' or 'anthropic' to the OpenAI branch via `else:` — a typo such as 'claude-cli' silently routes the judge to OpenAI with a model name like 'sonnet'. The non-default arms also construct a fresh anthropic.AsyncAnthropic() / AsyncOpenAI() per call and never close it (each owns an httpx connection pool) — the per-call client construction the briefing's thread/resource stability concern asks reviewers to flag; dormant under the shipped claude_cli config, live the moment a provider is switched.
findings.proposal: Type both fields as Literal['claude_cli','anthropic','openai'] (load-time refusal), give the provider axis one dispatcher shared by agent_loop and judge with an exhaustive match, and hold one SDK client per provider for the process lifetime. Structural (two modules).

findings.statement: Heuristic 13 symptom (a function-local import placed to break a cycle) plus a private reach. inject_operational_routing does `from fused_memory.middleware.task_interceptor import TaskInterceptor` inside the function ('Lazy import breaks the task_interceptor↔guard cycle') in order to call the private staticmethod TaskInterceptor._inject_deterministic_pure_gate. task_interceptor imports operational_routing_guard at module top, so a 140-line leaf guard depends upward on the 7,417-line class. It is one of several metadata helpers homed privately on the interceptor and consumed across modules. server/tools.py imports the privates `_is_ticket_id` and `_looks_like_task_id` from task_interceptor, and takes TERMINAL_STATUSES from task_interceptor's re-export of shared.task_statuses.TERMINAL rather than from shared. The pure-gate stamp (and its helpers _fresh_metadata_copy / _extract_metadata_dict) is pure metadata logic with no interceptor state.
findings.proposal: Move _inject_deterministic_pure_gate, _fresh_metadata_copy, _extract_metadata_dict, _is_ticket_id and _looks_like_task_id down to public functions in a lower module (deterministic_task_guard / a task-metadata helper module). Import TERMINAL from shared directly. The lazy import then goes away.

findings.statement: INV-8 loop-thread-occupancy-bounded: for every candidate with a non-empty module set, _build_corpus calls `self._taskmaster.get_tasks(project_root)` with no status filter and walks the result several times. That means up to batch_max=5 candidates per worker batch via prepare_candidate, plus curate()'s own rebuild. The live dark_factory store holds 6,525 task rows and 33.5 MB of description+details+metadata (counted read-only against .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, 2026-10-09). SqliteTaskBackend.get_tasks fetches rows on aiosqlite's thread, but the per-row _row_to_task conversion (JSON metadata parse) and the per-task files_to_modules matching run on the event loop. The collection is bounded by nothing but project growth, and the INV-8 question (numeric bound × per-item cost) is answered nowhere. The same full-tree read backs TaskInterceptor._check_escalation_idempotency (R4), whose docstring calls it 'authoritative and cheap' (heuristic 1) while it loads every row to match two metadata keys. INV-11 sibling: a get_tasks failure in _build_corpus is logged at DEBUG and leaves the module stream empty, so pool_sizes['module']=0 looks the same as 'no overlap'. Latency was not measured here; the claim is the unbounded on-loop fan-out, which the briefing's key decision forbids for reconciliation.
findings.proposal: Give the curator a narrow store read: a projection of id/status/files for non-cancelled rows (cf. get_statuses_raw), or a module->task index kept current at write time, and an indexed metadata lookup for R4. Surface corpus-stream failure in PoolWithheld/pool_sizes instead of DEBUG. Structural (new backend read or index).

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: the curator's pre-LLM pipeline order (blocklist -> premise -> claim-flag -> exact-match -> cache -> route -> ZOT breaker -> LLM -> degraded-create) is encoded twice, once in curate() (258 lines) and once in curate_batch_prepared() (338 lines, cognitive 82). The batch copy juggles three index spaces (original i, unique k, LLM-local j), and the two copies have already diverged. The batch path never calls _pre_llm_exact_match (its only call site is curate()). curate() documents that exact-match must run before the idempotency cache because 'a cached create decision is stale if the first caller has since landed the task', yet the batch path checks _check_cache directly. Its comment states 'Mirrors curate()'s precedence (blocklist -> premise -> exact-match -> cache -> route)', which is false (heuristic 1: a comment that lies). The impact is bounded: a stale cached 'create' served in a batch can still be caught at insert by the candidate_key partial UNIQUE index (DuplicateCandidateKeyError -> combine in _dispatch_ticket_decision), hence weakened. The next guard added to the curator must still be inserted correctly into both copies.
findings.proposal: Express the per-candidate pre-LLM stages once as an ordered list of stage functions (candidate -> decision|None) that both paths run; the batch path then only owns dedup-by-hash, LLM batching and index remapping. Structural (re-shapes the curator pipeline).

findings.statement: INV-11 / INV-4: the three curator registry guards (cancelled-premise blocklist, recon-premise registry, operational-ask registry) load once through _LazyRegistry.entries. utils/safe_yaml.py::load_yaml_list_file returns [] with one WARNING for a missing, unreadable or unparsable file, and a to_thread failure sets entries=None 'failing open (guard disabled)'. Either way `_attempted` latches for the process lifetime ('No hot-reload — a server restart is required'), so a typo'd path or a bad YAML edit disables that dedupe/routing guard until the next restart. Curator decisions look exactly like those of a healthy curator with an empty registry. startup_self_check checks only the claude binary, get_curator_state exposes no registry health, and no counter or escalation fires (INV-4: who hears about it when the fallback fires 100 times? nobody).
findings.proposal: Distinguish 'configured but failed to load' from 'loaded, empty': record a per-registry load status, report it from startup_self_check through the existing CuratorEscalator and from get_curator_state, and re-attempt on a later call instead of latching a failed load.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement plus heuristic 6 (purpose statable without 'and'). (1) Prose: 43.2% of 7,417 lines (metrics). (2) Partition: TaskInterceptor spans lines 432-6043 (5,612 lines, about 80 methods), and its docstring 'Wraps Taskmaster operations, intercepts state transitions for targeted reconciliation' describes perhaps a third of it. A self-attribute AST walk gives four families. Status transitions (935 lines) touch _write_lock, the journal helpers, _make_event, reconciler, idempotency and the consolidation collaborators. Path-scope guarding (926 lines, _path_guard_or_skip 230 + 19 helpers) touches only _prefix_registry, _scope_violation_escalator and _path_scope_adjudicator. The ticket/curator pipeline plus updates and reads (3,075 lines: worker, _dispatch_ticket_decision 262, _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared 381, _execute_combine 308) touches nearly all state. Wiring/lifecycle accounts for 543 lines. A further 1,374 lines follow the class: done-provenance validation, git probes, reopen-freshness and error builders. h13 symptom per candidate. Path-scope -> a PathScopeGate class owning its three collaborators: none (no back-reference needed). Module-level done-provenance block -> its own module: none (it references only its own helpers and config; tests patching task_interceptor._resolve_commit_committed_at / _run_hook would retarget). The ticket pipeline or status family as a satellite: a cycle. A ticket_worker module needs TaskInterceptor._write_lock / _curator_lock / _journal_around, so it would import task_interceptor while task_interceptor imports it to start workers. That split is legitimate only after the lock registry, journal and event emitter become a lower shared object both import.
findings.proposal: Extract PathScopeGate and the done-provenance gate module first (both symptom-free), then introduce a TaskWriteContext (locks, journal, event emit) below the interceptor before separating the ticket pipeline from status transitions. Structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 asks for invariants enforced 'at construction and at use'. TaskInterceptor instead takes 13 optional collaborators (each None meaning 'byte-identical legacy behaviour') plus four post-construction setters. Those setters are set_write_journal, set_lifecycle_reset_filer, set_audit_trail_archive and set_consolidation_scroll, and each arms a gate that is otherwise 'DORMANT': the consolidation-closure done-gate, the recon live-task-write self-check, audit-trail rotation, and client_op_id idempotency (_idempotency_replay silently returns None with no journal). Whether a status gate runs therefore depends on server/main.py::run_server remembering a call (heuristic 7: temporal coupling on prior calls). _wire_closure_collaborators's docstring concedes 'a future construction arm could still forget to CALL this helper'. run_server builds the interceptor in two arms with different collaborator sets. The reconciliation-disabled arm passes no bulk_reset_guard (the task-918 done->pending reversal circuit-breaker), backlog_policy, event_queue or lifecycle filer, so a status-transition safety gate varies with the unrelated reconciliation.enabled flag (heuristic 3). Other wiring reaches past interfaces: TicketJanitor is handed the private `task_interceptor._signal_ticket_event`, the reconciler gets `targeted.task_interceptor = task_interceptor` assigned after construction, and server/tools.py silently builds `TaskInterceptor(None, None, EventBuffer(db_path=None))` with no gates when given None.
findings.proposal: Construct the interceptor from one required, frozen collaborator bundle built in one place (both arms share it; gates that are safety-relevant are not optional); replace setters with constructor arguments; expose the janitor signal as a public method/callback; make the tools.py fallback a hard error. Structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 and heuristic 1: 'is this task a gate?' has four non-identical predicates and no named home. TaskInterceptor._is_gate_metadata (private staticmethod): always_escalates is True OR operational_mode == 'gate' OR execution_class == 'operational'. recurring_gate_guard.is_gate_submission: execution_class == 'operational' AND operational_mode defaulting to 'gate'. reconciliation/gate_owned_finding_phrasing.py's selector: always_escalates or operational_mode == 'gate', deliberately without the execution_class clause, with a paragraph headed 'WHY TaskInterceptor._is_gate_metadata IS NOT IMPORTED'. reconciliation/curator_gate_resolution_sweep.extract_open_gate_task_ids: operational_mode == 'gate' only. Each difference is defended in prose that cites the private predicate ('That citation is what keeps the duplicated boolean honest'), so the gate taxonomy (pure deterministic gate, human gate, operational submission) lives in comments, not types. 'Gate' means a different set of tasks at each site, and the next change to gate metadata (e.g. a new operational_mode) must find all four by reading prose (Comments stance: escalating prose standing in for a missing abstraction).
findings.proposal: Name the distinct concepts as public predicates in one module (e.g. is_pure_gate, is_human_gate, is_operational_submission) over a parsed TaskMetadata, and have the four sites call the one they mean. Structural (introduces a shared taxonomy).

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 (SPOT) and INV-5 no-lockstep-duplication: the shape and conditional requirements of done_provenance are enforced in two homes. shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py::DoneProvenance is a pydantic model whose _check_conditional_requirements already requires commit for kind in (merged, found_on_main), note for found_on_main, and escalation_id + note for operational-verified. _validate_done_provenance (409 lines, cognitive 82) never calls DoneProvenance.model_validate. It derives only the kind list from the model (_DONE_PROVENANCE_KINDS via get_args) and then re-implements the rest by hand: field-type checks ('kind must be a string', 'commit must be a string', 'note...', 'escalation_id...'), then `if kind == 'merged' and commit_input is None`, `if kind == 'found_on_main' and commit_input is None`, `... and note is None`, and the operational-verified escalation_id/note arms. A third copy of the kind axis sits in _apply_status_transition's `_verified_provenance = ... kind in ('merged','found_on_main')`. The model's docstring says kind is the single valid-kinds declaration (I2). The conditional rules are not single-sourced, so adding a kind or tightening a requirement must be done in lockstep at the server chokepoint and in the model readers use (heuristic 3: the per-kind axis is scattered if-arms).
findings.proposal: Parse at the boundary: DoneProvenance.model_validate(raw) and map ValidationError to the existing done_provenance_invalid dict (codes unchanged), keeping in this function only what the model cannot know: actor authorization, git resolution and ancestry, and stamped_at. Move per-kind behaviour (needs commit, verified-on-main) onto the model as properties.

findings.statement: INV-8: EventQueue.enqueue (labelled '# enqueue (sync, non-blocking)') now calls EventJournal.append, a stdlib sqlite3 INSERT + commit under synchronous=FULL — a per-commit fsync — on the event-loop thread, for every task-status transition: middleware/task_interceptor.py::TaskInterceptor._journal calls self.event_queue.enqueue(event) inline, and its docstring still claims 'the MCP hot path never awaits SQLite' (true of `await`, false of blocking — h1, the docstring now misleads). event_journal.py's module docstring sizes the cost at ~1-5 ms, i.e. the typical case; INV-8 asks for the worst case, which for an fsync under disk pressure is unbounded, and the shared/tests/loop_blocking_allowlist.py rows for event_queue.py cover only the dead-letter file I/O (task 6085), not this commit. INV-5 / h11 at the same class: EventJournal._apply_pragmas hand-mirrors the pragma triad ('Same durability triad as shared.async_sqlite_base.apply_full_durability_pragmas ... Kept in sync with that helper') with its own _JOURNAL_* constants, although shared/src/shared/sqlite_sync_base.py::apply_full_durability_pragmas_sync exists for exactly this (sync connection) case and is used by server/recon_report_store.py and topic_cluster_store.py.
findings.proposal: Call apply_full_durability_pragmas_sync (mechanical). For the loop occupancy, choose between offloading the journal commit (making enqueue async or handing off to a dedicated writer thread with a bounded queue) or recording an accepted INV-8 disposition with a measured worst case — a design choice, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12/10: the guard whose docstring says absence flags 'must be validated ... before Stage 2 can act on them, because delete_memory is irreversible' routes on LLM-emitted strings matched non-uniformly. flag_dedup defines five flag-type vocabularies (STALE_METADATA_, STALE_BULK_GET_STATUSES_, ABSENCE_, PHANTOM_TASK_CREATION_, AUTHORSHIP_SUSPICION_FLAG_TYPES); only STALE_BULK goes through canonical_flag_type_family (case/separator tolerant), the other four use exact frozenset membership. In filter_false_absence_flags a drifted spelling ('Task-Absent', 'task_missing') or an absence flag without task_id is passed through unchanged — it skips the fail-closed deletion guard and reaches Stage 2 (INV-11: the bypass is invisible). Absence itself is confirmed by substring-matching the phrase 'no tasks found for id' inside str(exc) of our own backend's TaskmasterError (confirm_task_absent) — an ad-hoc parser of an internal error message. Also heuristic 6/1: flag_dedup.py (6,021 lines, 0.60 prose) is named for dedup but hosts 13 public filter_* guards plus suppression writes and marker acknowledgment.
findings.proposal: One flag-type normaliser at the Stage-1 output boundary used by every guard; the absence guard fails closed on unknown absence-like types and missing task_id; the task backend raises a typed TaskNotFound instead of a phrase. Structural (boundary parse spans modules).

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement protocol for reconciliation/harness.py (6,529 lines). PROSE FIRST: prose_ratio 0.49; 217 task-number references and 28 review/amendment references; _run_remediation_pass alone is 866 lines with 415 comment lines; blocks such as run_full_cycle's ~25-line 'WHY THE GUARD' paragraph, the 'WHY BEFORE STAGE 3 / WHY AT THE TOP / WHY THIS IS SAFE' block, 'Reviewer finding race_condition:' and 'Known trade-off (task 2146 review follow-up)' on ReconciliationHarness.stages are reviewer-answering prose (Comments stance). PARTITION (ReconciliationHarness: 68 methods, 33 __init__ attributes, none first assigned outside __init__ — h5 clean): (1) module finding predicates + storm-finding dicts (_derive_affected_ids.._finding_is_live_actionable) → none; (2) run-failure record helpers + *_ledger_write_missing predicates → none; (3) diagnostics reads (_fetch_filtered_task_tree, _fetch_task_count_census, _check_graphiti_queue_health, _check_index_health, _detect_index_drift, _reconcile_status_correction) → none if escalation is passed as a callable; (4) cycle-summary backstop cluster (_reattempt_cycle_summary_write.._ensure_stage2_cycle_summary, _persist_stage_reports_then_gc_config_dir, ~660 lines) touching only self.memory/self.journal → none, cleanest extraction; (5) escalation filer (_escalate, _file_finding_task_escalation, _finding_recently_resolved, fingerprint scans, escalation-server start/stop) → none; (6) startup recovery (_recover_stale_runs.._record_resume_failure): _resume_interrupted_runs calls self.run_full_cycle and self._escalate, so a satellite would need `from fused_memory.reconciliation.harness import ReconciliationHarness` — reach-back unless run_full_cycle is injected; (7) remediation cluster (_backlog_state, _maybe_remediate, _run_remediation_pass, _finding_persistence_count, _get_prior_s3_findings, ~1,590 lines) references ~25 harness members (_make_stages, _configure_consolidator, _flush_cycle_summaries, _spawn_judge, _escalate, ...) — a split is stitching; (8) BacklogIterator already separate but reaches harness privates _known_project_scope_for/_escalate (h7); its function-local import of ContextAssembler breaks no cycle (gratuitous). The second 'deferred' import is the module-level try/except escalation-package import.
findings.proposal: Rehome reviewer-answering prose first; extract clusters 4, 5, 3, 1, 2 (symptom none) as downward layers taking memory/journal/escalate collaborators; leave 6-7 until run_full_cycle and stage configuration are public seams. Structural; chooses a partition.

findings.statement: Heuristic 7 (temporal coupling) with a loss path: BacklogIterator.run calls buffer.drain_by_ids (status='drained', drained_by_run_id NULL), then journal.record_chunk_boundary, then run_full_cycle, which only later calls mark_drained_run_id and journal.start_run. A crash or shutdown cancellation in that window (CancelledError is not caught by the iterator's `except Exception`) leaves rows drained, unattributed and with no run row: _recover_stale_runs restores only for an existing stale run, and once the project's reconciliation lock is gone EventBuffer.cleanup_drained (the only DELETE FROM event_buffer, every ~50 s) deletes `status='drained' AND timestamp < now-1h` — backlog events are old by definition — so the events are destroyed unprocessed, surviving only as rollup counts (INV-11). The iterator's failure path calls restore_drained(project_id) with no run_id — the project-wide form task 2711 scoped away from. Heuristic 1: restore_drained's docstring asserts 'every current code path now always stamps drained_by_run_id on drain', contradicted by drain_by_ids/mark_drained_run_id in the same file.
findings.proposal: Mint the run id before draining and drain-and-attribute in one EventBuffer call (as drain(run_id=) already does); restore by run_id. Changes the run_full_cycle(events=) contract — structural.

findings.statement: Tests stance: fused-memory/tests read 57 distinct private ReconciliationHarness attributes 717 times across 19 files (_escalate 94, _make_stages 58, _escalation_queue 45, _run_remediation_pass 34, _recover_stale_runs 34, _fetch_filtered_task_tree 33) and patch 13 names by dotted path into the harness module (write_stage2_cycle_summary 16, write_stage1_cycle_summary 13, _sleep 10, precheck_scope_correction_freshness 9, gc_run_config_dir 9, HAS_ESCALATION 4, ...). Production carries a `stages: list[Any]` attribute that exists so tests can assign harness.stages = harness._make_stages(scope) (its own comment: 'couples dozens of test call sites to the private _make_stages signature'); EventBuffer ships _debug_get_deferred_row as a test-support API; flag_dedup has 10 private names patched by dotted path and 22 private names imported by tests. The seams the tests reach through (stage construction, escalation sink, clock) are the missing interface.
findings.proposal: Constructor-inject stage factory, escalation sink and clock; drive tests through run_full_cycle/run_loop; co-moves with the harness extraction (FMR-10). Structural.

findings.statement: Scenario 'write deference during full cycles' (targeted._fenced_add_memory → EventBuffer.defer_write → claim_deferred_writes → _replay_deferred_writes). INV-7: a replay that raises leaves its row claimed 'so it isn't retried in this process'; the only release is release_stale_claims(0) at startup, so a deferred completion-knowledge write is held for the rest of the process lifetime with no bound or surfacing, and after _MAX_DEFERRED_WRITE_ATTEMPTS restarts it is DELETED with only logger.error (INV-11). Heuristic 11: replay calls memory.add_memory without causation_id (the immediate path passes it), so write-journal rows for replayed writes carry causation_id=None while the value survives only as metadata['_causation_id']; the stored agent_id column is returned by the claim and never used. INV-5: the done-dedup query pins categories=['observations_and_summaries'] and query text 'by hand to match the writer in targeted.py:_on_task_done' with a 'Keep these in sync' comment.
findings.proposal: Release failed claims on a bounded in-process schedule and escalate exhaustion; replay through the same fenced writer passing causation_id/agent_id; share the completion-write category/query constant with targeted.py. Structural (two modules).

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: the run lifecycle is implemented twice, by run_full_cycle and _run_remediation_pass — start_run → per-stage loop with the pre-integrity_check _flush_cycle_summaries → complete_run → verify_and_rewrite_stats → update_run_stage_reports → _spawn_judge, with three parallel except arms (CancelledError / AllAccountsCappedException / Exception) each hand-building run.stage_reports['_error'] (the AllAccountsCappedException dict literal is byte-identical in both). The copies have diverged: on CancelledError run_full_cycle honours config.resume_after_restart (marks 'interrupted') while the remediation pass always marks 'failed'; they escalate under different categories (recon_integrity_issue vs recon_failure). Heuristics 2/4: _run_remediation_pass is cognitive 101 (file max), 866 lines, defines two nested async closures over five pass-local inputs, and nests for-finding → if persistence → if any_live/else → if/elif/elif/else target routing. Heuristic 12 at the same seam: run.stage_reports values are StageReport OR dict (skip-all-fresh path writes {'items_flagged': ...}; '_error' is a dict), so the pass branches on isinstance(s3_report, dict).
findings.proposal: One run-lifecycle driver parameterised by run_type and stage list, one typed failure-record constructor, one value type for stage_reports; remediation's escalation routing becomes its own function. Structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 13/9: reconciliation/prompts/__init__.py is a 1,351-line fragment library living in a package __init__ (the 3 reach-back imports flagged by metrics: prompts/stage1.py imports 11 names, stage2.py 12, stage3.py 4 from their parent package; no cycle, since __init__ imports no stage module). render_recon_report_tool_guidance holds a function-local UPWARD import of fused_memory.server.recon_report (a 3,932-line server module that itself imports fused_memory.reconciliation.citation_repair and services.memory_service — reconciliation ⇄ server), and server/recon_report.py::get_recon_report_tool_signatures builds a throwaway FastMCP server and reads FastMCP privates (mcp._tool_manager._tools[name].fn). Because stage1/2/3 interpolate get_recon_report_tool_guidance() into module-level f-string constants (STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT etc.), merely importing a stage prompt module constructs a FastMCP server. INV-5: the fallback is a hand-maintained _FROZEN_RECON_REPORT_SIGNATURE_SPECS duplicate of the 10 tools' signatures kept honest by a drift test; INV-11: when the live render fails the caller silently receives the frozen (possibly stale) guidance with only logger.exception. Comments stance: get_recon_report_tool_guidance, _frozen_recon_report_tool_guidance and _cached_recon_report_tool_guidance carry ~100 lines of docstring/comment defending laziness and caching (task-2559 amendment, 'reviewer robustness finding').
findings.proposal: Move the tool-call specs to a small leaf module both server/recon_report.py (registration) and the prompts import — a declared spec the server registers from, rather than introspection of a built server — which deletes the frozen copy, the upward import and the import-time server construction; move the fragment library out of __init__.py. Structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 plus a defect: BaseStage._build_mcp_config needs the URL of the fused-memory server the stage runs inside — reconciliation requires server.transport='http' (server/main.py::_require_http_transport_for_reconciliation) and that server's own config holds host/port (8002) — but _find_fused_memory_server derives it from a CLIENT config file instead, trying a hard-coded user path Path('/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.mcp.json'), then cwd/.mcp.json. When neither yields an entry (missing/corrupt file is only warned via load_json_or_warn), it falls back to a stdio entry `uv run --project fused-memory python -m fused_memory.server.main`, i.e. the Claude CLI spawns a SECOND fused-memory server; server/main.py::main calls _acquire_singleton_lock() unconditionally, which SystemExit(1)s while the live server holds '\0fused-memory-singleton'. The stage then runs with no fused-memory MCP tools and nothing in the stage result says so (INV-11). The hard-coded home path also ties the stage to one host/user layout.
findings.proposal: Pass the server's own http URL (from config.server host/port) into the stage at construction and delete the .mcp.json discovery and stdio fallback; or refuse loudly when no URL is resolvable. Mechanical once the URL source is chosen; touches harness→stage construction, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 7 (temporal coupling) / heuristic 5: the stage's per-cycle inputs arrive by attribute assignment, not call arguments. MemoryConsolidator declares 11 class-level None attributes 'set by harness before run()' (episode_limit, memory_limit, remediation_findings, prior_s3_findings, cycle_fence_time, assembled_payload, filtered_task_tree, task_count_verification, graphiti_queue_health, index_health, status_correction_reconciliation) which harness.py::ReconciliationHarness._configure_consolidator assigns after _make_stages; harness also writes stage.filtered_task_tree for IntegrityCheck directly, and _propagate_escalation_queue writes the PRIVATE attributes s._escalation_url / s._escalation_queue into every stage. run() thus depends on a prior sequence of writes in another module, and a forgotten assignment silently reads the class-level None.
findings.proposal: Pass a frozen per-cycle input record (plus the escalation handle) into the constructor or run(); drop the class-level None defaults. Contract change across harness and three stage classes — structural.

findings.statement: Scenario 'Stage 1 → Stage 2 post-flight guards' — the chain runs here, not in the harness ('terminal-state pre-check' and 'snapshot discipline' are mostly prompt rules in prompts/stage1.py, backed in code only by filter_terminal_metadata_flags and task_count_snapshot_cadence). Heuristic 3: the post-flight axis has no mechanism. run is 1,142 lines (~525 code, ~585 comment; cognitive 100) and hand-sequences eleven flag filters (filter_stale_count_snapshot_corrections, filter_terminal_metadata_flags, filter_stale_bulk_get_statuses_flags, filter_already_tracked_systemic_patterns, filter_style_only_authorship_flags, filter_accounted_cluster_growth_flags, filter_already_recorded_caveat_flags, filter_benign_sweep_deletion_flags, filter_entity_standing_decisions, dedup_flags, filter_false_absence_flags), each with a hand-rolled `_before_X = len(...)` / `report.stats[...] = _before_X - len(...)` idiom and ORDER semantics (before/after the _pre_filter_flags snapshot, before/after dedup_flags — deciding whether a drop is acknowledged as resolution or kept as suppression) stated only in prose ('Position is load-bearing in both directions'); then ~13 further independently headed post-flight subsystems (preservation-specimen guard, curator-gate sweep, orphaned-escalation sweep, census inconsistency, task-count cross-verification, queue health, index health, status-correction reconciliation, stale-operator detector, gate-backlog check, degenerate-node sweep, status-snapshot edge sweep, priority-override edge sweep, cycle-summary write) each with its own fail-soft arm — purpose not statable without 'and' (h6, h4). INV-11: filters return bare lists, so suppression vs resolution is re-derived by three signature-set diffs ('The two causes cannot be told apart by this diff — dedup_flags returns only a list'). Heuristic 1: the comment 'Every sibling filter in this chain publishes its drop count' is false — filter_terminal_metadata_flags and filter_false_absence_flags publish none.
findings.proposal: A guard/post-flight pipeline: each step a value declaring its phase (pre-snapshot / pre-dedup / post-dedup / post-flight) and returning a typed result (kept, dropped-as-resolved, dropped-as-suppressed, stats); the runner publishes stats and computes acknowledgment. Rationale to the PRD/commits. Structural.

findings.statement: Convention 'All task state operations route through fused-memory MCP tools … TaskInterceptor must see every state transition' (heuristic 10: the invariant is enforced only by where callers happen to go, not by the layer). server/main.py hands the RAW task backend (`taskmaster = await _build_task_backend(...)`) to ReconciliationHarness, and Stage 2's `_maybe_queue_briefing_refresh_tasks` → `_queue_briefing_refresh_tasks` calls `taskmaster.add_task(...)` directly on it. Tasks it creates ('Refresh briefing: remove task N from known_gaps') therefore get no task_created event, no curator ticket / combine-or-drop dedup, and none of the submit-time guards the `submit_task` tool runs (lock-charter, premise-lint, routing, gitignored-deliverable …); its only dedup is an exact title match against pending tasks, from a full `get_tasks` tree read when the harness did not inject one. The path is gated to an allowlisted project (reify-specific per its docstring) and swallows every exception as a WARNING, so a misfiling is invisible. Heuristic 9: a lower-layer stage holds the storage backend the middleware layer exists to wrap.
findings.proposal: Give the recon harness the interceptor-facing task API (or a narrow 'file a task' port that goes through submit_task's guard chain and the curator) instead of the raw backend, so no reconciliation stage can write tasks around the interceptor. Changes a wiring contract — structural.

findings.statement: INV-11 + heuristic 4 + Comments: the function is 654 lines (215-line docstring, 150 comment lines, ~249 code; cognitive 92) with 9 keyword parameters, one (enum_filters) accepting dict | Sequence[dict] | None and one (terminal_task_ids) where None and [] carry opposite meanings the docstring calls load-bearing. It returns a bare int, so failure is indistinguishable from 'nothing stale': a get_memories_by_metadata failure logs a warning and returns 0; hitting scroll_limit returns a partial count with only a log line; retained_unclosed and protected-record skips exist only in WARNING logs. The docstring admits the KEEP-direction leak ('a persistently growing count means this pool needs a closure path') but that count reaches no caller.
findings.proposal: Return a frozen result (deleted, enumerated, truncated, enumeration_failed, retained_unclosed, protected_skipped) folded by the 4 callers into report.stats; rehome the measurement prose. Contract change across callers — structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12: task status — structured state the task store owns — is projected into Graphiti as free-text edge facts and recovered by a hand-built English grammar: _build_snapshot_patterns compiles five extraction paths (INDIVIDUAL_SNAPSHOT_RE, GENITIVE_STATUS_RE, SNAPSHOT_STATUS_PHRASE_RE, PLURAL_ENUM_SNAPSHOT_RE, LIST_INTRODUCER_RE) twice (union and blocked families) from regex fragments for copulas, adverbs, transitive-verb exclusions and enumeration separators, to decide which edges assert a now-stale status. The sweep itself writes its replacement as another sentence, _SUPERSEDE_FACT_TEMPLATE = 'As of {date}, task {task_id} has status {status}.' (status passed as a str), feeding the same prose channel the parsers read. Comments stance: AST measurement — 2,293 lines, 935 comment lines + 811 docstring lines + 205 blank, only 426 code lines (18.6%); the module docstring's 'Standing invariants' and per-constant blocks carry amendment history ('amendment, reviewer_comprehensive precision finding, task 3042'), repros and measurements — reviewer-answering prose the stance homes in commits/PRD.
findings.proposal: Stamp structured (task_id, status, as_of) attributes on status-snapshot edges/memories at write time and retire them by query, leaving the regex grammar as a migration sweep for legacy facts; rehome the rationale prose. Chooses a design — structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 'uniformly': the rule that reconciler task writes pass through the TaskInterceptor (write lock + status gates) is enforced three different ways because task_interceptor is attached post-construction as an Optional attribute (None in __init__; server/main.py assigns targeted.task_interceptor only after task_interceptor.start()): _on_task_blocked falls back to a direct self.taskmaster.update_task that bypasses the per-project write lock and gates (its comment says it keeps existing unit-test fixtures working — a production branch kept for tests), _sweep_cancelled_descendants and _unblock_dependent warn-and-skip, and three other sites assert not-None. Status transitions in the startup window before wiring skip the sweeps. Heuristic 7/13: targeted.py imports the interceptor's private helpers _extract_metadata_files and _missing_files from middleware/task_interceptor.py, while task_interceptor imports reconciliation.event_buffer/consolidation_gate/audit_trail_rotation at runtime — middleware and reconciliation are peers importing each other's internals.
findings.proposal: Inject the interceptor (or a narrow write-port protocol) as a required constructor argument; delete the direct-taskmaster fallback and give tests a fake port; move the two file helpers to a shared utility. Changes construction order in server/main.py — structural.

findings.statement: Scenario 'task status changes trigger targeted reconciliation — completion knowledge written, dependents get memory_hints'. INV-11: _on_task_done has six fail-open arms; five (fast-path completion write, flag-marker retirement, knowledge search, planned-episode promotion, step-3 dependency check) only log a warning and write no run_action row, and reconcile_task then journals the run 'completed'. Its result dict reaches no caller: task_interceptor.py::_apply_status_transition launches it fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task and _on_reconciliation_done only logs exceptions. So if get_tasks fails in step 3, blocked dependents whose deps are now all done are never re-pended (the reify 5662/5759 defect _sweep_unblock_dependents exists to close) and nothing durable records it; the only backstop is the orchestrator's stranded-blocked redispatch, where an orchestrator runs (stability_concerns[0] shape). INV-8 / key decision 'recon must not load the full task tree on the event loop': step 3 calls get_tasks(project_root) for the whole tree on EVERY done transition to find one task's dependents, though TaskBackendProtocol offers get_dependency_edges and get_statuses (live dark_factory: 6,525 rows, 13.8 MB metadata JSON; JSON decode alone measured 0.096 s on the loop per transition). Heuristic 1 against the briefing: memory_hints are written only onto a newly BLOCKED task (_on_task_blocked), never onto dependents in _on_task_done.
findings.proposal: Record a run_action (or partial status) per fail-open arm so the journal distinguishes 'completed' from 'completed with skipped steps'; find dependents via get_dependency_edges + get_statuses; correct the briefing scenario via /review-briefing. Structural.

findings.statement: INV-11 on step 1 of the add_memory scenario (two-tier classification when category=None): WriteClassifier._llm_classify returns primary=observations_and_summaries when the OpenAI call raises (confidence 0.3) or returns no JSON (0.4), and classify() also falls there when the heuristic misses and llm_fallback is off. MemoryService.add_memory reads only classification.primary and discards confidence/reasoning, so an OpenAI outage silently re-routes every unclassified write that should go to Graphiti (entities/temporal/decisions) into Mem0; AddMemoryResponse.category reads as a normal classification, the only trace is a logger.error, and no counter/streak alarm exists (INV-4).
findings.proposal: Carry a classification_degraded flag through ClassificationResult into AddMemoryResponse and add a storm counter on LLM-classifier fallbacks.

findings.statement: Tests stance, anchored at the module reached into. fused_memory.server.main is the slice's most-patched module (12 distinct private targets per patch-targets.txt). Tests rebind module globals and privates: `_operator_stop_received` (×8, test_asgi_exception_shield), `_LOOP_LAG_INFO_EVERY`, `_LOOP_LAG_INTERVAL`, `_loop_lag_iteration` (test_event_loop_lag), `_run_rebuild_summaries_cycle`, `_acquire_singleton_lock`, `_cancel_force_exit`, `main_mod.os._exit`, `_HARNESS_CANCEL_TIMEOUT`, `signal`, `logger`. The seam is the defect. Process lifecycle state is module-level mutable globals (heuristic 5): _operator_stop_received, _shutdown_watchdog, _watchdog_thread, _watchdog_stop_event and _singleton_socket. The bootstrap is one 824-line run_server with 21 function-local imports that does argument parsing, journal pruning, guard/escalator/registry construction, two duplicated interceptor-wiring arms, janitor, checkpoint, rebuild and lag loops, both uvicorn servers and teardown (heuristic 4; heuristic 6 fails the one-sentence test). Several of those imports serve neither cycle-breaking nor laziness: TaskInterceptor and EventBuffer are already loaded through main.py's top-level import of server.tools, which imports task_interceptor at module top (heuristic 13 symptom without a reason). Vestigial branches remain. `try: await taskmaster.start() ... except: 'will retry on next tool call'` guards a no-op start() that cannot fail. `'event_buffer' in locals()` / `'ticket_store' in locals()` guard names bound in both arms. _janitor_primary_root recomputes _primary_root.
findings.proposal: Make the process lifecycle an object (ServerProcess holding stop flag, watchdog thread, singleton socket, tunables as constructor args) and split run_server into build_components(config) -> Components (one wiring path) and serve(components); tests then drive those seams with real fixtures instead of rebinding globals. Structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement, done per the protocol. (1) Prose: 52.0% of the file's 10,561 lines are prose (metrics), and the tool docstrings alone are 138,169 chars (FMT-16). (2) Partition: 89% of the file (lines 1176-10561, 9,386 lines) is one function, create_mcp_server, holding 62 @mcp.tool closures and 28 helper closures. The remainder is constants, override/park-eviction DB helpers, update_memory arm validation and paging helpers. Its reported cognitive complexity of 1233 is mostly nesting of closures: extracted standalone, the 90 closures sum to 742, with maxima consolidate_memories 73, add_memory 69, delete_memory 36, _citation_repoint_gate 31 and commit_planning 31; 12 closures exceed 15. Measured capture sets give a partition by tool family. Scheduler-override tools (482 lines) capture only _normalize_project_root, a pure function that need not be a closure. Task tools (1,759) capture task_interceptor, _kp, _log_read, _normalize_project_root and _reject_if_ticket_id. Memory reads (916) capture memory_service and _log_read. Graph edits (781) capture memory_service, _known_project_gate and _verify_mint_referent. Ops tools (813) capture the harness, queues and gates. Memory writes (2,538) capture memory_service, topic_cluster_store and the 14 cascade/citation/claim gate closures (_citation_repoint_gate alone is 402 lines). h13 symptom per candidate: none for every family module, provided the shared closures (_log_read, _backlog_gate, _known_project_gate, _halt_payload, _normalize_project_root) move to a lower context module that the family modules import downward. Moving the closures as-is would force each family module to import those helpers back from fused_memory.server.tools (a reach-back into the parent), so a naive split is the cheat the doc forbids. Tests stance: because the helpers are closures with no seam, tests reach into the module namespace instead. `fused_memory.server.tools.resolve_main_checkout` is patched 26 times so that _normalize_project_root can be steered, along with _open_park_eviction_db, judge_write, group_search_results and _RELOAD_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS.
findings.proposal: Replace the closure with a small ToolContext (frozen deps + the shared helpers as methods) in a lower module and one register_<family>_tools(mcp, ctx) per family module; move the memory-write gate closures to their own module taking memory_service explicitly. Tests then construct a ToolContext with fakes instead of patching module names. Structural (split, per contract §6).

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: fused-memory's MCP layer is a second writer of the orchestrator-owned scheduler_overrides.db and carries hand copies of its contract. These include _OVERRIDE_SCHEMA ('intentional duplicates of orchestrator.overrides._SCHEMA'), _PRIORITY_TIERS (a copy of orchestrator.config's tiers) and _VALID_CLEAR_FIELDS (mirrors OverrideStore.clear_override). set_task_priority_override (162 lines) re-implements the pin-order auto-assign and collision check in raw SQL under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, in parallel with orchestrator's OverrideStore/PinOrderCollision. The pin 'Source of truth: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/overrides.py:33-49' is already stale: the schema now sits at lines 37-53. The schema text is byte-identical today, so this is drift risk, not live drift. The DB path is derived three times in fused-memory despite _overrides_db_path's 'Single source of truth' docstring: tools._overrides_db_path, reconciliation/stale_priority_override_edge_sweep.py and scripts/cleanup_pin_queue_edges.py. The stated reason ('adding an orchestrator dependency would invert the dependency graph') is answered by shared/, which fused-memory already imports (shared.task_statuses, shared.async_sqlite_base). Heuristic 9: the store has two owners in two packages, not one owner below both.
findings.proposal: Move the override store (schema, tier vocabulary, path, set/clear/pin-order logic) into a shared/ module and have both orchestrator and fused-memory call it. Structural (cross-package ownership change).

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 (structured data instead of meaningful strings; no routing on string prefixes): caller role, the input to several write-authority decisions, is never parsed. _resolve_identity returns the raw agent_id string (caller-supplied or clientInfo.name), and every consumer re-derives 'is this a recon stage' by prefix. `git grep "startswith('recon-stage-')"` finds 23 literal sites in fused-memory/src, including tools.py ×8 (e.g. _extract_causation, add_memory), task_interceptor ×2 (is_recon_stage_write in _apply_status_transition and update_task), execution_class_guard, premise_lint_guard and recurring_gate_guard. Meanwhile two named homes exist (reconciliation/internal_writers.py::INTERNAL_WRITER_AGENT_ID_PREFIXES and flag_record_contract._RECON_STAGE_AGENT_PREFIX), config/schema.py repeats ['recon-stage-', 'curator-'] as three default_factory lists, and shared.task_transitions.derive_actor_class is a fourth classifier (heuristic 11). A change to the stage naming scheme, or a new privileged writer family, has no single place to land.
findings.proposal: Parse identity once at the tool boundary into a frozen CallerIdentity (agent_id, role enum: recon_stage / curator / orchestrator / interactive / unknown) from one prefix table, pass it through to guards and the interceptor, and delete the literal prefix tests. Structural (crosses guards, interceptor and config).

findings.statement: Comments stance. FastMCP sends each tool's __doc__ as its MCP description (mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py: `func_doc = description or fn.__doc__`, and no tool passes description=), so tools.py's docstrings are an agent-facing contract. They total 138,169 chars (about 34.5k tokens) across 62 tools: consolidate_memories 183 lines, add_memory 167, get_statuses 144, submit_task 127, update_task 99. Much of that is maintainer- and reviewer-facing prose shipped to every client. get_statuses tells agents '(Deliberately no line numbers above: these symbols live in three other packages ...)' and 'The rule for future maintainers, stated as an invariant', and lists out-of-process consumers in three other packages. Inline, submit_task carries a 72-line reviewer-answering block ('COST, MEASURED', 'NAMED RESIDUAL 1/2'); main.py::_wire_closure_collaborators has a 45-line docstring for a 10-line body ('RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than papered over'); and run_server points into an escalation record ('tracked as a follow-up to task 3088 (escalation agent-followup-3088)'), which the doc says does not count as a home. The prose has also drifted into a lie (heuristic 1). update_task's description tells agents to 'Prefer structured fields (title, description, details, priority, status, dependencies)' and documents `status: New status (e.g. "pending"/"in-progress"/"done")`, yet SqliteTaskBackend.update_task raises StatusWriteAuthorityError for every non-None status, and TaskInterceptor.update_task's docstring lists that floor as gate '1. ... (run in order)' when it actually runs last, after idempotency, directory-lock, backlog and recon-policy checks.
findings.proposal: Treat tool descriptions as the agent contract: keep them to purpose, arguments, return shape and errors; move rationale to docs/ (pointer from code) and measurements/defences to commit messages or task records; fix update_task's description (state that status is rejected and name set_task_status) and the interceptor gate list. Structural only in breadth (many sites), no design choice.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement protocol for services/memory_service.py (11,323 lines). PROSE FIRST: 6,040 lines docstring/comment (53.3%), 978 blank, 4,305 code; the MemoryService class is 9,070 lines, 4,650 prose; 212 task-number references. PARTITION with the h13 symptom per candidate: (P1) module-level write-metadata policy L420-1314 (_infer_recon_pool, cycle-summary tagging, _normalize_task_id_metadata, _apply_memory_metadata_validation, _check_canonical_uniqueness, ~895 lines) — takes collaborators as injected callables; symptom none. (P2) referent wire codec / result conversion / store-failure diagnostics L1318-1869 (~550) — symptom none; today reconciliation/preservation_specimen_guard.py imports private _mem0_content and server/grouped_read.py imports private _MEM0_CONTENT_KEYS from this file, which a split would give a public home. (P3) episode-identity post-write pipeline L2878-5837 (2,937 lines, 22 methods + ReferentRepair/ReferentRepairStats/DescendantScan) reading self.graphiti/taskmaster/_write_journal/_known_projects and owning four _referent_* counter dicts; one inbound call (_execute_graphiti_write → _reconcile_episode_identity) and one outside write (_referent_source_counts[...] += 1): symptom none as a composed class with injected backends, reach-back into MemoryService private state (fails h13) if split as a mixin/function-bag over self. (P4) queue execution + terminal/dead-letter plumbing (~760 lines): imports P3 downward, none as a class; its payload contract would cross the boundary as bare operation strings (see FMR-3). (P5) hierarchy/cascade delete L8859-9321 (~460): none. (P6) graph-mutation API L9805-11258 (~1,450) with entity-mint storm state: none as a class over graphiti+journal. Remainder (write API ~1,000, read API ~2,000) stays as façade. The two function-local imports break no cycle: initialize imports PlannedEpisodeRegistry (already TYPE_CHECKING-imported; that module imports no fused_memory module) and get_memory imports Scope (already imported at module top) — gratuitous.
findings.proposal: Rehome the prose first; then P1-P6 as downward layers, with P3/P4/P6 as composed classes (never mixins). Structural; chooses a partition.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 / INV-5: the durable-queue operation vocabulary ('add_episode', 'add_memory_graphiti', 'mem0_classify_and_add', 'mem0_add') is bare string literals held in agreement across four modules. Producers: add_memory ('add_memory_graphiti'), _dual_write_callback ('mem0_classify_and_add'), replay_from_store. The dispatcher _execute_durable_write tests two names and sends ANY other string to _execute_graphiti_write, so a typo'd or new operation silently runs as a Graphiti write; durable_queue.py::DEFAULT_IDENTITY_PAYLOAD_KEYS keys on 'add_episode'; middleware/dead_letter_escalator.py::_REPORTED_TO_CALLER is kept in step only by a comment ('A new enqueue site ... must add an entry here'). The TEXT `operation` column's meaning has no single home.
findings.proposal: One StrEnum in durable_queue (TEXT-compatible) used by producers, an exhaustive dispatcher that raises on unknown values, the identity-key map and the escalator claim table. Structural (four modules).

findings.statement: Comments stance + heuristic 4: _verify_episode_referents spans 728 lines of which 527 (72%) are docstring/comment (cognitive 84). The ~150-line docstring and inline blocks are PRD-leaf narration ('leaf gamma… leaf epsilon… leaf ETA… leaf iota', 'Resolved decision 7', 'its absence is not an oversight'), task history (5262, 3671) and placement defences ('ordering is load-bearing') — reviewer-answering prose the stance homes in the PRD/commit. The ~180-line executable body does five things (build ambiguity set with a legacy re-derivation arm, index nodes, walk edges×endpoints with two ordered checks, resolve intended uuids, count/log/journal). MemoryService.search has the same register: 453 lines, 246 prose ('PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING', 'COMMIT POINT'), routing + fan-out-with-timeout + RRF sort + category filter + topic-anchor pin + telemetry journalling in one body (cognitive 81).
findings.proposal: Rehome rationale to the referent-verification PRD with a one-line pointer; split the body along its five steps (edge×endpoint classification is a pure function over (edges, names, referents, ambiguous, known_projects)); same for search (fan-out, merge, pin, telemetry). Structural.

findings.statement: Scenario 'add_memory is retrievable via search' — the response contract names a fact it does not establish (heuristic 1) and carries store failure only as prose (heuristic 12). On the Graphiti leg add_memory appends SourceStore.graphiti to `stores_written` as soon as durable_queue.enqueue returns ('Durably persisted to SQLite — report as written') while the same response's message says 'Memory queued for [...]'; middleware/dead_letter_escalator.py::_REPORTED_TO_CALLER records the consequence ('the caller was told this write LANDED, not that it was queued'). A store exception is caught into _graphiti_error/_mem0_error and spliced only into `message` ('[graphiti_error: ...]'); AddMemoryResponse (models/memory.py) has no error/degraded/queued field, so consumers infer failure from absences — server/write_triage.py::attach_write_landed treats an empty memory_ids as not-landed (≈25 docstring lines defending the inference), which is wrong for Graphiti-primary categories whose memory_ids is empty even on success. INV-11: a degraded write is indistinguishable from success in the value the caller receives. (Routing itself is SPOT: models/enums.py GRAPHITI_PRIMARY/MEM0_PRIMARY; search carries degraded/failed_stores correctly.)
findings.proposal: Give AddMemoryResponse a structured per-store outcome ({store: written|queued|failed, error_class, error}) plus a top-level degraded flag; rename/retire stores_written; have write_triage and tools read it. Wire-contract change — structural.

findings.statement: INV-5 / heuristic 11: the memory-hierarchy 'child' rule (kind in {amendment, sighting} AND a non-empty str parent_id) has three definitions of its kind set and two hand-mirrored implementations of the rule. memory_metadata.py::CHILD_KINDS (the normative vocabulary module, already imported at module scope by services/memory_service.py) defines it; server/grouped_read.py re-defines CHILD_KINDS from its own AMENDMENT_KIND/SIGHTING_KIND literals; services/topic_anchor.py::_CHILD_KINDS restates frozenset({'amendment','sighting'}) a third time with a comment claiming it is 'DELIBERATELY restated rather than imported from server/grouped_read.py' because 'a services -> server import here would close an import cycle' — true of grouped_read, but memory_metadata exports the same constant with no cycle (memory_service already imports it), so the rationale is wrong and the duplication needs a pinning test (tests/test_topic_anchor.py::test_child_kinds_matches_the_grouped_read_registry, comparing only two of the three copies). The rule itself: server/grouped_read.py::_parent_id_in_meta implements it, server/write_triage.py::_canonical_id_of re-implements it inline ('mirrors grouped_read._parent_id_in_meta rule-for-rule'), and reconciliation/stages/memory_consolidator.py imports the PRIVATE _parent_id_in_meta upward from the server layer (h13/h9); grouped_read in turn imports the private _MEM0_CONTENT_KEYS from services/memory_service.py.
findings.proposal: Home CHILD_KINDS, PARENT_ID_KEY and a public parent_id_of(meta) in memory_metadata.py; have grouped_read, write_triage, topic_anchor and memory_consolidator import it; delete the pinning test. Spans four modules — structural, though no design choice remains.

findings.statement: stability_concerns[1], any swallow around SetTaskStatusRejected, plus INV-6 status-matches-liveness. In the slice there are 19 'except Exception' arms with no re-raise wrapping a scheduler.set_task_status call: 8 in harness.py, 4 in workflow.py and 7 in deterministic_runner.py. Each swallows the SetTaskStatusRejected family, including TerminalExitRejection, together with transport errors. Five of the runner's sites are one copy-pasted tail across _file_infra_issue_and_block, _file_stop_instruction_and_block, _file_curator_adjudication_missing_and_block, _file_milestone_gate_and_block and _file_milestone_check_failed_and_block. Each copy is commented 'Same rationale as ...', logs a WARNING and 'returns BLOCKED regardless'. When the write fails, the slot exits reporting BLOCKED while the row is still in-progress with no live claimant. That is the shape INV-6 forbids, and recovery is left to the reconcile sweep's escalation-pinned LEAVE/convert path. A rejection is folded into the same arm as a severed connection, so a gate verdict (for example, the task is already terminal) cannot be told apart from an outage at the point of consumption.
findings.proposal: Route all exit-status writes through one helper that distinguishes SetTaskStatusRejected (handled per subtype, as workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._repend_for_requeue already does) from transport failure, and that records the failed write in the result (as _note_exit_status_write does for the run()-exit contract). Replace the five runner tails with one call. This is mechanical within the runner; extending it to harness and workflow spans modules.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 plus heuristic 4. DeterministicRunner.run is one 1,212-line method (36 return statements, 525 comment lines). It dispatches on the raw task metadata dict, with 37 metadata.get/before_done.get reads in the module. Branching keys include before_done.get('kind') == 'predicate', gate_escalated_at, always_escalates and the curator-gate marker. A typed pydantic model, shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py::BeforeDone, already exists and is validated at the write boundary. The runner parses none of it, so its branches re-derive kind from strings, and the comments spend paragraphs defending against combinations the model already rejects ('Task 3369 landed the durable fix ... This WARNING is deliberately KEPT'). The two axes, resume versus first dispatch and gate kind (pure gate, predicate, deploy, curator), are handled with inline flag checks inside a single method rather than one mechanism per axis (heuristic 3).
findings.proposal: Parse metadata into the shared BeforeDone/TaskMetadata models at the top of run, then dispatch to one method per (phase, kind) pair through a table or match statement. Move the defensive-history prose to the task or PRD records. The work is confined to one module but restructures it.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 and heuristic 11, on the dry-run proposal record behind codebook investigator-context-and-budget. metadata.dry_run_proposals entries are untyped dicts assembled by hand at six sites in dry_run_unblock.py: _build_entry's budget_exhausted, infra_failure, investigation_failed and success returns, the unexpected-error arm, and _cap_exhausted_entry. Every site writes the same instant under two keys, 'investigated_at' and 'timestamp'. The success entry omits 'status' and 'cost_usd', so consumers must read 'no status' as success. The readers re-derive the schema independently. agents/briefing.py::BriefingAssembler._format_prior_proposal reads proposal.get('timestamp') or proposal.get('investigated_at') and compares it to metadata.last_blocked_at as ISO strings, failing open on a parse error. b3_gate.py reads 'the latest dry_run_proposals entry from tasks.db' directly. The unblock-low-risk skill keys on dry_run_proposals[-1].risk_label. A field rename at any producer silently changes what the retry and resume prompts feed forward.
findings.proposal: Define one frozen DryRunProposal model (status enum, risk_label enum, files_referenced, cost_usd, investigated_at as a datetime) in a shared module, used by every producer and parsed at every reader (briefing, b3_gate). Drop the duplicate timestamp key after a read-both migration. The change spans orchestrator modules and a skill.

findings.statement: INV-8 loop-thread-occupancy-bounded: EventStore.emit is synchronous and, per event, opens a new sqlite3 connection, applies the full durability pragma set (journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=5000 ms, synchronous=FULL, wal_autocheckpoint, journal_size_limit), INSERTs, commits with an fsync, and closes. It is called directly from coroutines on the orchestrator's event loop at ~140 call sites in orchestrator/src (none offloaded), including per-task-per-tick fan-outs such as Scheduler._note_external_hold and _note_delivered_hold, whose count is the number of pending gated tasks. Worst case per emit is the 5 s busy wait when another process holds runs.db's write lock, multiplied by the fan-out. The repo's INV-8 ratchet (shared/tests/test_loop_blocking_gate.py) deliberately scopes itself to fused-memory/src, so nothing measures this in orchestrator.
findings.proposal: Make emit non-blocking for async callers (an in-process queue drained by one writer thread with a persistent connection, or asyncio.to_thread at an async emit), keep a sync variant for non-loop callers, and bound per-tick emit fan-out. Changes a widely-used interface, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement (15,857 raw lines). Prose first: 6,440 docstring + 2,807 comment lines = 58.3% of the file, much of it history of removed code (the 40-line module docstring on retired .task/ guards) and reviewer-answering defences (e.g. create_worktree's 25-line rewrite note inside the FAULT RuntimeError, 'Task 4930 rewrote this message ...'), which belongs in commit/task records. Then the partition: almost everything is one class, GitOps (lines 2871-15857, ~200 methods), whose purpose cannot be stated without 'and' (heuristic 6: worktrees and warm-lane pool and merge-verify leases and commit-effect probes and train stacking and main advancement). An AST scan of self-method calls between method clusters gives: (a) commit-effect probes (describe_commit_effect_in_main .. commit_effect_present_in_main, ~1,380 method lines, owns _effect_probe_memo) call only get_main_sha — symptom none; (b) main advancement (advance_main, recover_red_main, push_main, index-lock stand-off, WIP park ref, ~1,330 lines, owns _index_lock_path_cache and the _last_* side channels) calls only _detect_unmerged_paths, get_main_sha, resolve_queued_branch_ref — none once those primitives sit in a lower layer; (c) train stacking (~360 lines) delegates to branch_stack — none; (d) warm-lane lifecycle (~3,600 method lines plus ~1,500 module-level lines of warm-lane enums, exceptions and the lane-lock fd registry) is two-way coupled: create_worktree calls acquire_warm_lane/_reuse_warm_lane/_provision_reify_debug_port/_relocate_foreign_meta_root while the warm-lane cluster calls _is_registered_worktree/_repair_orphaned_reuse_lane, and cleanup_worktree calls release_warm_lane/release_spec_lane while the cluster calls cleanup_worktree/quarantine_base/_prune_registrations — a warm_lane_ops module split today would import git_ops.GitOps back (cycle via cleanup_worktree <-> release_warm_lane); (e) persistent merge lanes <-> merge (_create_merge_worktree vs is_persistent_merge_lane) also cycle and should stay together. So (a)-(c) are legitimate splits now; (d) needs the worktree-registry primitives moved down first.
findings.proposal: Extract commit-effect probing, main advancement and train stacking as their own classes/modules over an injected git runner (see SVG-8); move worktree-registry primitives (_is_registered_worktree, _prune_registrations, quarantine_base, cleanup_worktree's non-pool core) into a lower module, then lift the warm-lane lifecycle out beside warm_lane_pool.py. Rehome history prose to commit messages. A split, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 7 (stateless interactions) and heuristic 5: advance_main returns a frozen AdvanceOutcome value object, yet the file lists that explain its 'wip_overlap' and 'stash_failed' results travel through instance attributes it assigns mid-call (self._last_overlap_files, self._last_stash_dirty_files; also _last_park_lock_info, _last_recovery_branch), which orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_lane/gates.py reads afterwards with getattr(git_ops, '_last_overlap_files', None) / getattr(git_ops, '_last_stash_dirty_files', None). That is another module reaching into private attributes and relying on call order: the values are never reset, so a reader on a later call path sees whatever the last advance left, and the getattr default hides a renamed attribute as an empty list in the escalation text. Tests pin the side channel too (26 referencing lines across test_git_ops.py, test_merge_gates.py, test_merge_queue.py, test_atomic_train_merge.py).
findings.proposal: Carry overlap_files / dirty_files / park_lock_info / recovery_branch as fields of AdvanceOutcome and delete the instance attributes; gates.py reads the outcome. Small, but it changes a cross-module result contract, so structural.

findings.statement: Convention '.task/ directories must never be committed to main' now rests on a premise the code contradicts (heuristic 1, prose that lies, plus heuristic 10: the invariant is enforced at zero runtime points). git_ops.py's 40-line module docstring says .task/ contamination is 'structurally impossible ... nothing ever writes task metadata into a path git tracks', that the hot path 'no longer writes task metadata under <worktree>/.task', and that 'No .task-specific guards remain in this module'; GitOps.commit's docstring says `git add -A` 'has nothing under .task/ to stage'; advance_main documents the retired _assert_no_task_dir tripwire as a trade-off justified by that premise. But the hot path writes inside the git worktree's .task/: workflow.py constructs TaskConfigDir(base_dir=self.worktree / '.task') (per-task Claude config incl. .credentials.json and session transcripts; harness.py and GitOps.cleanup_worktree read it at <worktree>/.task/claude-config-<branch>), ensure_lane_plan_symlink creates <worktree>/.task/plan.json, and verify.py::_mark_verify_warm writes verify_warmed* markers there (and _is_verify_cold treats '.task/ exists' as 'is a task worktree'). GitOps.commit runs `git add -A -- . :!.claude` and ignores the add's rc, so the only remaining barrier for an operated repo is that repo's own root .gitignore (DF's hooks/pre-commit applies only where core.hooksPath resolves to DF's hooks). Meanwhile merge_to_main still rmtrees a .task dir 'belt-and-braces', workflow.py's '.task/ contamination guard' comment says 'create_worktree() should have scrubbed' (it no longer does), and the root .gitignore comment still lists four defences (commit pathspec + post-staging check, merge scrub, advance_main hard gate) that git_ops says were removed — INV-9 drift. Related: create_worktree unconditionally runs `git config --replace-all core.hooksPath hooks` on every operated project's shared repo, a DF-specific assumption applied fleet-wide.
