Coordinator verification (weakened from high): every live operated git repo checked at review time (dark-factory, reify, pump-web-ui, know-live, autopilot-video, scoping-intake, solar-challenge-platform) ignores `.task/` in its root .gitignore and /factory-init mandates that entry, so nothing stages today; the cost is the false prose and the single remaining barrier, which now also guards a per-task `.credentials.json`.
findings.proposal: Decide the invariant's enforcement points and make the prose match: either move TaskConfigDir and the warm markers under the meta root so the 'nothing under <worktree>/.task' premise becomes true, or restore one cheap mechanical check (commit-time or advance-time 'tree has no .task/ entries') and add `:!.task` to commit()'s pathspec; then rewrite the git_ops/.gitignore/workflow prose to describe what exists. Make the hooksPath assertion conditional on project config. Chooses between designs, so structural.

findings.statement: Tests stance and heuristic 1: git_ops._run is the repo's de-facto public async subprocess primitive under a private name. Ten production modules besides git_ops use it — scheduler.py (git_ops._run), delivered_checks.py (as the default injected runner), workflow.py, merge_lane/{gates,disposition,landing_evidence,worker,skew_tripwire}.py, verify.py, and escalation/src/escalation/server.py across a package boundary — five of those via function-local imports (verify.py three times, skew_tripwire, escalation server) although `import orchestrator.git_ops` does not load orchestrator.verify, so no cycle requires them (heuristic 13 symptom; skew_tripwire's says it 'mirrors' verify's lazy import). GitOps methods call the module global directly and GitOps takes no runner, so tests can only intercept by patching 'orchestrator.git_ops._run' (230 occurrences in 22 test files), and 120 test files import _run (150 sites, mostly to drive real git in fixtures). The docstring meanwhile names a different seam ('git_ops.run_git is the single patchable spawn seam').
findings.proposal: Publish the primitive under a public name in a small lower module (or use shared.git_async directly), import it at module top where no cycle exists, and inject a runner into GitOps at construction for tests that need to fake git; keep real-git fixtures on the public name. Cross-package rename, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement protocol, harness.py (18,264 lines). PROSE FIRST: 9,017 prose lines (49.4%). The prose includes 470 'task NNNN' mentions, 25 review-answering markers ('review finding', 'reviewer_comprehensive', 'review amendment/fix') and 14 escalation-record pointers. In the hottest functions it is the majority: _reconcile_one_stranded is 65% prose and _run_slot 61%. Rehoming that reviewer-answering prose (Comments stance) would still leave about 9.2k code lines, so prose alone does not explain the size. PARTITION of top-level symbols, with the h13 symptom each part would hit: (P1) the module constants and free predicates (_pid_alive, _recon_inspect_unit, _deterministic_*_stranded, _is_terminal_merged, _has_fresh_*, _acquire_project_lock; about 820 lines). Symptom: none, since they reference no Harness member; 5 private names are imported by tests from orchestrator.harness. (P2) build_train_callback_factory plus _TRAIN_MEMBER_READY_STATUS (390 lines). It uses only that constant and the logger from harness, so the symptom is none. Its natural home, merge_lane, already sits in the workflow cycle (HWA-4), and its twin TaskWorkflow._revert_withheld_member should join it (HWA-2). (P3) the watcher-supervisor group (8 methods, 561 lines, plus the _WATCHER_* constants). It owns _watcher_unclean_exits, _watcher_degenerate_clean_exits and _watcher_supervisor_task, and calls 4 Harness methods (_filing_claimant_run_id, _maybe_write_digest, _scan_for_terminal_active_tasks, pause_scheduler). Symptom: none if those are injected callables; a reach-back if they are extracted as functions over harness. (P4) the recovery/reconcile group (36 methods, 4,356 lines, 28 Harness data attributes, 10 out-of-group calls). Extracted as functions over Harness it would need 'from orchestrator.harness import _RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES, Harness', closing the cycle harness -> stranded_reconcile -> harness. It passes only as an owned component with injected scheduler, git_ops, ground truth and escalation queue, with its constants moving with it. (P5) the escalation-filing group (27 methods, 2,047 lines, 39 data attributes). Symptom: reach-back unless a filer object owns the queue, event_store and claimant id. (P6) the resolution cascade (_on_escalation_resolved, _cascade_unblock_member, _action_teardown_and_set_status and others; 6 methods, 1,120 lines, 8 attributes). Symptom: none with injected scheduler and queue. (P7) the digest group (2 methods, 325 lines). Its counters _escalation_event_count and _escalation_submit_count are mutated by _on_escalation, so a split is a reach-back unless the digest owns the counters. The remaining ~6.6k lines (run, _run_slot, dispatch gates) stay. The file is a flat bag of peers inside one class rather than strata (h9).
findings.proposal: Split along P3, P6 and P4, in that order, as owned components (not function bags), each passing h13. Move P1 and P2 downward. Record the measurement in the task record. A split is structural by definition.

findings.statement: Tests stance plus heuristic 9. Harness is a 16.6k-line class with 189 methods and more than 71 instance attributes, built in a 529-line __init__, and it has no narrow constructible seam. Tests bypass the constructor with 'Harness.__new__(Harness)' 37 times in 17 files and then set private attributes by hand. Production code has bent to accommodate this: harness.py has 23 getattr(self, ...) and 5 getattr(self.config, ...) tolerance reads, and 9 comments that justify code shape by the __new__ fixtures. For example, _reconcile_one_stranded reads getattr(self.config, 'convert_to_blocked_enforce', False) 'for the same documented reason ... several narrow-scope test harnesses build a Harness via Harness.__new__(Harness)', and _emit_recovery_disposition and the lifecycle-registry builder say the same. A missing attribute in production then reads as a default instead of failing, and the tests never exercise the real wiring (heuristic 6: Harness is a process supervisor, a recovery engine, an escalation filer, a watcher supervisor, a digest writer and a dispatch-gate host).
findings.proposal: Extract owned components with constructor-injected collaborators, for example a StrandedReconciler, an EscalationFiler and a WatcherSupervisor (see the HWA-17 partition). Tests then construct those directly and need no Harness.__new__. Remove the getattr tolerances once no fixture bypasses __init__. This is a design choice spanning the module and its test suite.

findings.statement: Crash-recovery scenario ('recover WIP from surviving worktrees'). Heuristic 7: _recover_crashed_tasks (630 lines) reaches into GitOps private members. self.git_ops._lane_lifecycle is used 7 times across harness.py (read and transition), and self.git_ops._is_registered_worktree once. Other harness methods reach _on_pool_storage_absent, _orphan_has_commits, _run_warm_lane_gc_reclaim and _warm_lane_base_resolvable. The code even explains that quarantine is done in 'two explicit steps rather than lane_lifecycle.quarantine()' because 'git_ops captured quarantine_worktree at construction time, and tests ... replace the LIVE git_ops.quarantine_worktree'. INV-5: the record-driven path and the plan.json heuristic path each carry their own copy of the identity guard and quarantine, the completed-steps computation, the stamped-plan preservation and the plan.lock unlink. Cross-references between them are by stale in-file line pins ('~2394-2434 below', '~2322'). The copies have already diverged: the heuristic-path identity-mismatch quarantine neither transitions the durable lane record to QUARANTINED nor records 'dest' in the worktree_quarantined event. Heuristic 1: the docstring says it 'also resets any in-progress tasks to pending', but the body writes no status (that is _reconcile_stranded_in_progress).
findings.proposal: Give GitOps or WarmLanePool a public adopt_or_quarantine(entry, task_id, reason) that owns the lifecycle transition and event. Factor the per-worktree decision into one classifier that returns a typed disposition (adopt, preserve, quarantine, release, clean or defer) consumed by both paths. Fix the docstring. This is a mechanical fix within one function, but the GitOps API change spans modules.

findings.statement: INV-11, no-silent-fail-soft. harness.py wraps 'from escalation.queue import EscalationQueue; from escalation.server import create_server' in 'try/except ImportError: HAS_ESCALATION = False', and 'from orchestrator.steward import TaskSteward' (a first-party sibling module) in 'except ImportError: HAS_STEWARD = False'. Escalation is a declared hard dependency (orchestrator/pyproject.toml lists 'escalation' as a workspace dependency), and harness.py already imports escalation.classify and escalation.pins unconditionally at the top. The guard therefore never protects an absent package. It only converts a genuine ImportError inside escalation.server, escalation.queue or steward.py (a renamed symbol, a broken transitive import) into an INFO line ('Escalation package not installed - skipping escalation server') or a silently absent steward factory (_run_slot: 'if HAS_STEWARD and self._escalation_queue'). Either way the L0/L1 ladder, the steward and every 'if self._escalation_queue' filing site degrade to no-ops, and that cannot be told apart from a healthy run. Heuristic 13 symptom: harness.py also has 29 function-local 'from escalation.models import Escalation' imports that break no cycle (escalation/models.py imports only the stdlib).
findings.proposal: Delete both ImportError guards and import escalation.queue, escalation.server and orchestrator.steward at top level, so a broken import fails at startup. Hoist the 29 escalation.models imports to one top-level import. This is mechanical: one file, no design choice.

findings.statement: The plan-files gate's docstring promises 'Fail-open on git error ...: return an empty PlanFilesTouchedResult so a transient diff error doesn't block a real merge.' The body does the opposite. It calls git_ops.get_files_touched_in_branch(base_sha, branch_head), which returns [] on a 'git log' failure (git_ops.py::GitOps.get_files_touched_in_branch: 'Returns [] on git error so the helper fails open'). The gate cannot tell that [] from 'the branch touched nothing' (inv-11). Every declared plan file that exists in the branch tree then fails _entry_touched_exactly and lands in not_touched. The consumer, workflow.py::TaskWorkflow's merge-entry block, treats check.not_touched as the failing arm. It runs the narrowing and already-landed probes and otherwise blocks with plan_files_not_touched, which by key_decision short-circuits to L1 with a human escalation. A transient git error is therefore reported as 'the branch under-delivered', with the git rc/stderr fact lost (inv-2). Both docstrings misdescribe the behaviour (h1). The same [] reaches gates.py::_resolve_already_landed_branch's touched set.
findings.proposal: Make get_files_touched_in_branch return a distinguishable failure, either by raising or by returning (paths, error). In the gate, map that failure to the documented outcome: fail-open, or an UNCLASSIFIED entry as the ls-tree probe already does, with the git error carried in the result.

findings.statement: Train kind (declared by the workflow vs coalesced by the worker) is a real axis of variability, and MLANE-1/MLANE-2 are both its unpriced cost. It has no type: it is encoded as the string prefix _COALESCE_TRAIN_ID_PREFIX = 'coalesce-' inside train_id and routed on by train_id.startswith at three sites in worker.py (_stand_down_train, _dissolve_coalesce_trains_if_halted, the _merger_loop post-train hook). That breaks h12 (structured data instead of meaningful strings). The kinds differ in who consumes the outcome (a workflow awaiter vs no one), in restart recovery (re-dispatch of the tip task vs none), in derail recovery (_redrive_coalesce_members only for coalesce), and in halt ownership (only the declared consumer registers an owner). Verify-scope union is implemented twice with different semantics. workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._union_train_scope returns 'union_files or None' from member metadata.files. The worker's inline union in _maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles makes any member with task_files None widen to all files, and takes the tip's scope under merge_verify_workspace. Train-member selection (workflow.py::_select_train_members) is called from both sides. Per h3, each behaviour difference is a scattered inline check, not one mechanism, and every new train behaviour must remember to ask the prefix.
findings.proposal: Make the kind a typed field on GroupMergeRequest (an enum, or a TrainOrigin carrying its recovery and owner policy), set at construction. Route on it, not on the id. Give scope union and member selection one home in the lane, and have the workflow call it. Behaviour-preserving apart from the decision in MLANE-1/MLANE-2 on what coalesce trains should do at restart and halt.

findings.statement: Comments stance. Much of worker.py's 58% prose is task archaeology and reviewer-answering prose, not rationale that has to live in code. Counted in worker.py: 582 'task NNNN' mentions; 109 lines citing reviewer findings or amendments; 50 lines narrating removed or former code ('field deleted', 'formerly', 'pre-kappa', 'used to'); 28 repetitions of the same 'MQ-reliability kappa (task 2169)' annotation at each _retire_item site; and 4 pointers into escalation records, which the stance says do not count as a home. SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__ is 722 lines, 77% prose, for 168 code lines. _verifier_loop carries a 44-line defence of a deleted clause ('The clause is gone outright: tracing every path shows it was redundant...'), which is exactly the prose the stance assigns to the commit message. The drift risk is realised: _main_health_fingerprint's docstring asserts 'no module-level cycle' while the file's own import block imports orchestrator.workflow at module level (MLANE-4). Bare line pins are excluded from this count per CONTRIBUTING.md §2.
findings.proposal: When a region is next touched, move reviewer-answering and historical prose into the commit or task record, and move rationale that must persist into the PRD or a doc with a path pointer. Replace repeated per-site annotations with one invariant stated where it is enforced (for example _retire_item's own docstring). Do not do this as a standalone sweep (tolerated-drift rule). Do it with the structural work in MLANE-6/7.

findings.statement: Halt-owner state is not single-owner. h10 *uniformly* fails: set_lane_halt_owner and set_halt_owner assert there is no different owner, but halt_for_wip and operator_halt overwrite _lane_halt_owner[lane] = None on every lane, including a lane already halted by another owner. MERGE_LANES is ('high', 'normal'), and _pop_next_pickable skips only halted lanes, so the high lane keeps landing while the main-health auto-heal holds 'normal' (_maybe_auto_heal_main_health sets halt_lane('normal') plus set_lane_halt_owner('normal', esc_X)). A wip_overlap on a high-lane merge then calls halt_for_wip, which erases X. The workflow registers its own owner Y on all halted lanes via set_halt_owner. Resolution of X no longer releases 'normal', because harness.py::_on_escalation_resolved releases only when is_halt_owner(esc.id). Resolution of Y releases everything, ending the auto-heal halt early. unhalt_lanes_owned_by and lane_owned_by have no production callers. The mixin's purpose is not one sentence (h6): it holds per-lane halts, the operator halt (_operator_halt), 'legacy all-lanes shims', _abandon_outcome (a loop-breaker outcome builder) and _request_abandoned. It is a methods-only class whose state is created by SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__.
findings.proposal: Model halts as a per-source ledger, for example {lane: {source: owner}}, where a lane is runnable iff its ledger is empty and each source releases only its own entry. Fold operator halt in as one more source. Move the abandon helpers out. Delete unhalt_lanes_owned_by and lane_owned_by, or wire them.

findings.statement: The lane's module-level pipeline functions take the whole worker and reach into its private state (h7: no reaching into another entity's attributes). classify_and_merge, _advance_train, _do_train_merge, reverify_member_solo and _journal_landed_then_advance's callers make 29 'worker._*' accesses in worker.py. They read worker._git_ops and worker._event_store. They mutate the worker's per-task counters through worker._cas_retries, worker._post_merge_verify_timeouts and worker._post_merge_verify_enospc_retries, which are passed on as mutable dicts. They probe optional collaborators via getattr(worker, '_landed_outbox', None), getattr(worker, '_escalation_queue', None) and getattr(worker, '_flake_task_client', None). They call private worker methods: _note_conflict_detected, _build_merge_failure_diagnostic, _render_failure_diagnostic, _emit_speculative, _verify_frontier_depth. The interface type _TrainMergeHost declares those private attributes as its protocol. classify_and_merge branches three times on isinstance(worker, SpeculativeMergeWorker), and its own docstring says the other branch 'is now unreachable' since task 5034 discarded the serial worker's test-local copy. The capability split survives as dead code.
findings.proposal: Replace the worker parameter with explicit collaborators. A small frozen context (git_ops, event_store, outbox, escalation port) plus a counters object owned by one party should be passed in and returned as values. Delete the unreachable isinstance arms, and move the speculative-only behaviour into the caller that knows it is speculative.

findings.statement: Fourteen pre-package modules are re-export shims that replace themselves in sys.modules with a lane submodule (h13 symptom: 're-export shims'). They are merge_queue, merge_gates, merge_shadow, merge_liveness, merge_types, merge_disposition, merge_drift, merge_completion, merge_queue_store, merge_request_ledger, merge_skew_tripwire, merge_speculation_controller, landing_evidence and landed_outbox. Each does 'from orchestrator.merge_lane.X import *' and sets 'sys.modules[__name__] = X', with a stub module __getattr__. The shims are not kept only for tests. Production code imports through them: harness.py, workflow.py (mostly function-local), stranded_verified_green.py, suffix_graph.py, unblock_types.py, cross_repo_gate.py, dry_run_unblock.py, evals/live_fixture.py, task_ground_truth.py, escalation/server.py, escalation/git_authority.py and escalation/merge_lane_resolution.py. escalation/server.py imports the private orchestrator.merge_queue._resolve_dispatch_time_merge_base, and the façade's _EXPORTS table publishes '_resolve_dispatch_time_merge_base' beside the public name. On the test side, 139 test files reference orchestrator.merge_queue and 69 reference orchestrator.merge_types, and the string-path patches in MLANE-5 resolve only through these aliases. The shims' own docstrings name task 5037 as the migration-and-delete step.
findings.proposal: Execute task 5037 as planned: migrate production importers to the merge_lane façade (public names only; drop the private alias from _EXPORTS and give escalation a public entry point), then migrate tests off module-path patches (MLANE-5), then delete the shims.

findings.statement: INV-5 / heuristic 11, with measured drift: _pid_alive exists as six hand copies — orchestrator/session_registry.py, orchestrator/harness.py, orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py, shared/config_dir.py (whose docstring calls itself 'the fourth instance of that deliberate copy-don't-import pattern'), fused-memory/services/orchestrator_detector.py and scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py. They already disagree: session_registry's copy catches OverflowError for a pid too large for pid_t (its docstring: 'ordinary untrusted input, not a hypothetical'), the harness, task_ground_truth and shared copies do not and raise. The stated reason for copying (keep shared below orchestrator) runs the wrong way: shared is the lower layer, so orchestrator and fused-memory can import a shared definition; only session_registry's stdlib-only, run-by-path constraint justifies a local copy.
findings.proposal: Put one definition in shared (e.g. shared.proc_group) with the OverflowError handling, import it from harness, task_ground_truth, config_dir and orchestrator_detector, and keep session_registry's copy with a drift test against the shared one. Spans packages, so structural.

findings.statement: Heuristics 10 (clear invariants, uniformly enforced) and 1 (informative names). The steward_lifetime_budget ($12, config.py and defaults.yaml) is enforced against self.metrics.total_cost_usd, an in-memory StewardMetrics field of one TaskSteward. A steward is built per TaskWorkflow instance (workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._ensure_steward_started), so every re-dispatch of a task and every orchestrator restart starts a fresh $12 'lifetime'. That is inconsistent with the steward's other caps. Task 5352 deliberately made the retry, timeout, empty-output and capped-escalation guards durable per task (PersistentMap/PersistentSet under data/orchestrator/guards/<guard>/<task_id>.json) 'so a fleet redeploy no longer hands a record that already exhausted its ladder a fresh full budget'. The cost cap was not migrated. The name 'lifetime' therefore promises a per-task bound the code does not keep. routing_dispatch.py's docstring describes the applied per-invocation cap as 'min(config.budgets.steward, steward_lifetime_budget - spent)', where 'spent' is that same per-incarnation counter.
findings.proposal: Persist steward spend per task the same way as the other four guards (or read it from CostStore per task), so the cap is enforced uniformly. Otherwise rename the knob to per-incarnation and document the real bound. This is a choice between two semantics.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement (11,086 raw lines). Prose: 3,568 docstring + 2,371 comment lines = 53.6%; e.g. VerifyResult spends ~110 comment lines defending each field's JSON-native shape against its generic asdict / VerifyResult(**d) codec, and _scope_to_keyword carries ~60 lines of comment for a 15-line body. Partition by an AST scan of cross-cluster name references among top-level symbols: (1) command-string façade (_scope_to_keyword, _reproject_str, _cargo_scope_str, _serial_pytest_str, _with_*_str, ~750 lines) — one upward reference, _serial_pytest_str -> _worktree_reader (in the entry-point cluster); none once _worktree_reader moves down. (2) pytest output parsing and crash attribution (722-1413 plus the _PYTEST_*/_XDIST_* regexes defined near the top) — none. (3) summary/log/junit/archive persistence (2112-3074) — references only (1)/(2): none. (4) subprocess execution, cgroup scopes, env, admission, clock-stop (_run_cmd, _run_segmented, 4280-6366) — references only module head: none. (5) main-SHA failing-id baseline (1413-1744) calls run_verification/run_scoped_verification while verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main (8738, called only from merge_lane/worker.py and workflow.py) calls back into it — a split leaves a cycle verify_baseline <-> verify unless verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main moves with it, after which: none. (6) main-tip sweep and flake discrimination (8997-11086, ~2,090 lines) calls run_verification/run_full_verification, while run_verification calls its _load_sample/_xdist_workers (load sensing, belongs with (4)) and run_scoped_verification calls _emit_trivial_pass_escalated — cycle verify_flake <-> verify unless those three symbols move; then none. So every part passes heuristic 13 after moving four named symbols; the practical blocker is the Tests stance (SVG-7: 199 dotted patches of orchestrator.verify._run_cmd).
findings.proposal: After SVG-7's runner seam, split along (1)-(6) with the four moves named; rehome field-defence prose from VerifyResult to the codec (or replace the codec with an explicit from_wire). A split, so structural.

findings.statement: INV-2 structured-facts-at-failure: VerifyResult.failure_report — the block report handed to debugger agents — re-derives facts the emitter held in variables. Which commands timed out is recovered by `'timed out' in self.test_output.lower()` (and lint/type likewise), although each leg's CheckRun already carries timed_out: bool and rc — the emitter had the fact in a field; a type-check section appears only if `'error' in self.type_output.lower()`; lint output is a positional [-2000:] tail; worker-death truncation is re-detected by regex over test_output, and the inline comment says it is derived from the log 'rather than from a new dataclass field' because every field carries codec and compare= risk. That codec choice (result_from_dict = VerifyResult(**d), no parse at the boundary) is also why category is a plain str and failing_leg_categories a list[str] although FailureCategory is a StrEnum (heuristic 12). This class is the anchor of codebook entry block-report-misattribution (13 sightings); the failure-anchored excerpt (_failure_anchored_excerpt) fixed the test-tail slice, the leg attribution remains scraped.
findings.proposal: Carry per-leg outcomes (leg, timed_out, rc, category as FailureCategory, truncated_by_worker_death) as a typed field produced by run_verification, add an explicit from_wire that reconstructs enums, and render failure_report from those fields only. Changes the wire contract, so structural.

findings.statement: INV-5 / heuristic 11: verify.py::_scope_to_keyword and verify_plan.py::_scope_prefix_to_keyword are the briefing's 'kept in lockstep' pair. Both bodies run the same nine-step pipeline (split_chain_tail, find, keyword_truncation_end, parse_config_command, OPAQUE/raw bail-outs, has_unpreserved_chain_clauses + log_dropped_chain_clauses, scope_to -> promote_cwd_to_project -> strip_cwd, tail re-append); the shared helpers keep each step aligned but the sequence itself is duplicated, and each copy carries ~60-110 lines of docstring/comment restating the same tail-preservation and log-level policy (Comments stance), both asserting the lockstep is 'now STRUCTURAL'. Measured: over all 30 lint/type/test commands in the tree's eight orchestrator.yaml files plus three edge cases (value flag after target, cd fan-out chain, pinned npx@version), _scope_to_keyword(c, k, f) == render(_scope_prefix_to_keyword(c, k, f)) for every input (0 diffs), and verify_plan does not import verify, so the string scoper can be one call to the VerifyCmd scoper with no cycle. Until then a change to the scoping rule is two edits plus two docstrings.
findings.proposal: Replace the body of verify._scope_to_keyword with `None if cmd is None else render(verify_plan._scope_prefix_to_keyword(cmd, keyword, files))` (public-named), keep the policy prose once in verify_plan, and keep the existing byte-identity corpus test as the guard. No design choice.

findings.statement: Heuristics 3 and 4: run_verification is 993 lines (462 of them comment lines, cognitive 160) taking nine parameters including three booleans (allow_cold_cache, is_merge_verify, segment_chained_test) and role: Literal['merge','task','background']. The merge-vs-task axis is carried by two flags: is_merge_verify selects cold treatment, timeouts and warm-marker writes; role selects env, admission and junit attribution. Callers combine them inconsistently — merge_lane/gates.py and _merge_gate_isolated_rerun pass (role='merge', is_merge_verify=True), _probe_modules_on_main passes role='merge' without is_merge_verify and run_full_verification forwards its role parameter without one, the sweep rerun passes role='background' — so 'is_merge_verify=False' on a role='merge' run is legal and its meaning has to be reconstructed from the body (heuristic 1). run_scoped_verification (664 lines, 302 comment lines, cognitive 131) threads the same pair plus force_workspace.
findings.proposal: Replace the flag pair with one typed VerifyPurpose (or a small policy object built once from role) from which cold treatment, timeout, env and attribution are derived, then factor run_verification into plan-legs / execute / classify / persist steps. Chooses the axis model, so structural.

findings.statement: Verify-host selection, quarantine and fallback each have two homes (h11). VerifyRunnerPool carries a selection policy (prefer the first non-quarantined non-local runner), its own _quarantined set, an INV-2 sync-bench re-selection loop, and a RunnerUnavailable fallback to local. HostAllocator carries a different selection policy (verify_host_policy prefer_local/prefer_remote, read per call), the worker's _runner_quarantine set shared by reference with the worker and DriftDetector, and the PARKED state. The worker's _run_inflight_verify/_finalize_inflight implement the production RunnerUnavailable path by re-dispatching and counting a streak. In production every merge-verify pool is built single-runner: worker.py::_run_post_merge_verify builds [runner] or [LocalRunner(...)], and shadow.py builds LocalRunner only. The pool's selection, its _quarantined set and its 'fall back to local' arm are therefore inert on the merge path, and only merge_lane/drift.py builds a two-runner pool. VerifyRunnerPool.dispatch branches on isinstance(selected, RemoteRunner) twice, because the VerifyRunner protocol's run_merge_verify(merge_sha, spec) does not carry task_id/archive_root/event_store, which only RemoteRunner accepts (h9). It also imports logging and EventType function-locally. A reader changing 'how a verify host is chosen or benched' must find and keep consistent two policies and two quarantine sets.
findings.proposal: Give host selection and quarantine one owner, the HostAllocator. Reduce VerifyRunnerPool to the dispatch-and-emit transport over an already-chosen runner, or fold it into the allocator lease. Widen the VerifyRunner protocol so dispatch needs no isinstance branch. Keep the drift detector's two-runner comparison as an explicit caller of two leases.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement protocol, workflow.py (18,039 lines). PROSE FIRST: 8,293 prose lines (46%), including 333 'task NNNN' mentions, 40 review-answering markers and 19 escalation-record pointers. _drive is 53% prose and _mark_blocked 51% (its docstring includes a 'MERGE_PHASE_RATIONALE (Chesterton's-fence investigation)' git-log measurement). That is reviewer-answering prose under the Comments stance. PARTITION, with the h13 symptom for each part: (W1) the 35 module-level helpers (914 lines: _select_train_members, compute_preexisting_main_break_fingerprint, compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint, build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments, classify_rebase_cohort, _evaluate_*). Symptom: none. Moving them to a lower module REMOVES the existing cycle closed by merge_lane/worker.py's top-level 'from orchestrator.workflow import _select_train_members' (HWA-4). (W2) the merge/train group (47 methods, 4,971 lines, 29 data attributes, 31 out-of-group calls into _mark_blocked, _wait_for_resolution, _enter_phase and others). As functions over TaskWorkflow it is a satellite reaching back. It passes h13 only once the escalation result is a returned value (HWA-1, HWA-6). (W3) the steward/escalation group (17 methods, 1,276 lines, 16 attributes, 8 out-calls). Symptom: a reach-back into _mark_blocked, unless the HWA-11 protocol is redesigned. (W4) the plan group (7 methods, 782 lines, 14 out-calls). (W5) the execute/verify/review group (23 methods, 3,543 lines, 39 attributes, 42 out-calls). Its coupling runs through the stash attributes (HWA-6), so it fails h13 until those become return values. (W6) the recovery/terminal group (16 methods, 1,449 lines). (W7) the workflow_types re-export shim at line 159. The split is already done, and the shim itself is the h13 symptom (86 importing files). Unlike harness.py, most candidate parts fail h13 today because of shared mutable instance state, so a split now would be a cheating split.
findings.proposal: First do W1 (a downward move that breaks the cycle) and W7 (retire the shim). Make the W2, W5 and W3 splits only after HWA-6 and HWA-1 replace the stash and flag protocols with typed return values. Record the measurement in the task record. A split is structural by definition.

findings.statement: Tests stance: test access to a module's internals is an interface-design smell. orchestrator/tests contain 866 assignments to private TaskWorkflow attributes across 89 files. The most common are wf._invoke = ... (96), wf._mark_blocked = ... (81), _steward_factory (48), _base_commit (32), _reverify_one_member (30), _execute_verify_review_loop (26), _steward_outcome_channel (25) and _check_branch_on_main (24). There are also 58 patch.object(..., '_x') calls on harness/workflow privates. Separately, 'orchestrator.workflow._run' is patched 51 times. The seam those tests reach through is the real defect (h9): workflow.py imports git_ops's private subprocess runner _run (line ~102) and shells out to git directly 11 times (9 rev-parse) instead of going through its injected GitOps, so tests must patch the module namespace. The cost is concrete. HWA-1's RC2a defect survives because its only test replaces _mark_blocked with a mock, so no test drives a real _mark_blocked against a real escalation queue for that route.
findings.proposal: Route the 11 direct git calls through GitOps methods, which removes the _run patch target. Give TaskWorkflow narrow injected collaborators for the agent invoker, steward and escalation filer, so tests substitute those instead of private methods. Add integration tests that drive the real _mark_blocked and steward handshake against a real EscalationQueue on tmp_path. This is a test-architecture choice spanning many test modules.

findings.statement: Heuristic 7 (no temporal coupling between modules) and heuristic 10. The workflow and the steward synchronise through two different channels. _await_steward_completion (reached via _mark_blocked) reads an in-process asyncio.Queue. _wait_for_resolution (reached via run()'s ESCALATED branch) is woken only by a side effect: the steward dismissing its L0 in the escalation queue, then resolve -> _resolve_callback -> harness._on_escalation_resolved -> _escalation_events[task_id].set(). The invariant that keeps the second waiter from parking forever ('a steward give-up ALWAYS dismisses its own L0 before publishing an outcome') is enforced by prose, restated in the steward module docstring, _handle_escalation, _ensure_steward_started and _await_steward_completion. The steward docstring records that task 2248 shipped exactly that strand. INV-5: the defensive 'get_by_task(status=pending, level=0) then resolve(dismiss=True, resolved_by=auto-dismissed)' loop is hand-copied at four sites in workflow.py: _mark_blocked's skip_escalation branch, its StewardInterrupted branch, its BLOCKED fall-through, and the has_open_l1 override in _await_steward_completion. Each copy has different resolution text, and one of them is HWA-1's misleading 'after steward re-escalation'.
findings.proposal: Have both waiters consume one typed steward-outcome channel, with the dismissal performed by a single steward-owned give_up(outcome) that dismisses and then publishes atomically. Replace the four workflow loops with one helper that takes a reason. This chooses a synchronisation design.

findings.statement: Heuristic 5, minimum data access scopes and lifetimes. The verify, execute and merge legs return a bare WorkflowOutcome.BLOCKED (or None) and pass the reason through instance attributes, a pattern the code itself calls 'the stash idiom'. Examples: _infra_hold_info, _inherited_break_info, _zero_output_hang_info, _progress_resume_churn_info, _last_verify_result, _last_merge_block_reason/_failure_category/_failure_cause_hint, and _pending_resume_session_id/_role. Each is written by one method and read by exactly one other. Across TaskWorkflow, 45 attributes are mutated outside __init__. The stashed values are untyped dicts read by key (info['reason'], info['category'], info['fingerprint']). _infra_hold_info's 'category' and 'escalate_to_human' keys are written but ignored by the consumer, which hardcodes both. Correctness depends on read order ('Must be checked BEFORE _inherited_break_info to prevent ... clobbering'). _infra_hold_info is never reset after construction, unlike its siblings. _merge_recovery_basis exists only 'so tests can assert the MP-2 invariant directly against live workflow state'. A typed BlockDisposition already exists in workflow_types.py, so the stash duplicates a return channel that already exists (h7 temporal coupling: correctness depends on call order within one object).
findings.proposal: Have _verify_debugfix_loop, _run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry and _execute_iterations return a typed block verdict (BlockDisposition, extended with reason, detail, category, fingerprint and block_status) and pass it straight to _mark_blocked. Delete the stash attributes, and the test-only _merge_recovery_basis, in favour of an observable event. The change is confined to TaskWorkflow but touches many methods.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings. _submit_to_merge_queue routes a MergeOutcome on its human-readable reason prose. It makes six result.reason.startswith(<PREFIX>) tests (WORKTREE_MISSING, DROPPED_PLAN_TARGETS, POST_MERGE_EQUIVALENCE_FAILED, POST_MERGE_PYRIGHT_BROKEN, TRANSIENT_INFRA, MAIN_HEALTH_RED), then a substring sniff ('verification failed' in result.reason.lower()), and switches on result.status string literals ('superseded', 'conflict'). _maybe_enqueue_group_merge adds two more prefix tests (TRAIN_INCOMPLETE, TRAIN_VERIFY_FAILED). _mark_blocked enforces the spawn_dry_run ordering invariant with reason.startswith(POST_MERGE_PYRIGHT_BROKEN_REASON_PREFIX). The typed alternative already exists one branch later: MergeFailureDisposition.INTEGRATION_SKEW is read from getattr(result, 'disposition', None). The routing therefore uses two mechanisms for one axis. The prefixes are defined across merge_lane/gates.py and merge_lane/worker.py and re-exported through the merge_lane __init__ and the merge_queue alias, so rewording any reason prefix silently reroutes a drop-guard or main-red case into the generic 'task fault' path. That path is the briefing's 'drop-guard short-circuits to L1' scenario.
findings.proposal: Carry the gate verdict as a typed field on MergeOutcome (extend MergeFailureDisposition, or add a MergeBlockKind enum stamped where each prefix is minted today) and dispatch on it with an exhaustive match. Keep reason as display text only. This changes the MergeOutcome contract across merge_lane and workflow.

findings.statement: The lane does not sit below its client: worker.py imports upward into the workflow and scheduler layers. These are module-level imports in worker.py: 'from orchestrator.workflow import _select_train_members' (a private workflow name that is pure train-selection logic, used by the worker's coalesce pass), 'from orchestrator.scheduler import StaleEvidenceRejection' and 'from orchestrator.suffix_graph import ...'. The other direction is stitched with deferral. workflow.py makes 36 function-local imports into lane modules, for example 'from orchestrator.merge_queue import TRAIN_INCOMPLETE_REASON_PREFIX, ... register_and_enqueue_merge_request' inside the group-merge path. suffix_graph.py imports MERGE_LANES/MERGE_BOUNCE_CAP/NEEDS_REBASE_REASON_PREFIX back from merge_queue function-locally, 'required to avoid deadlocking merge_queue's re-export shim'. worker.py::_main_health_fingerprint makes a deferred import of workflow.compute_preexisting_main_break_fingerprint. Two documents now lie (h1). _main_health_fingerprint's docstring says the lazy import keeps 'merge_queue→workflow ... a deferred import (no module-level cycle)', while the module-level workflow import above it makes that false. types.py::TrainCallbacks describes the worker as 'a pure git engine with no scheduler import', while worker.py imports orchestrator.scheduler. This is the h9 nesting failure (a flat mesh where layering belongs) plus h13's cycle-breaking function-local imports. Same cycle seen from the workflow side (merged from the HWA seat's HWA-4): offline_lane.py also lazily imports compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint and build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments from workflow; workflow reaches the lane through 8 function-local imports from the deprecated merge_queue alias plus 3 from merge_lane; and workflow.py carries a declared '# noqa: F401 re-export shim' of 17 workflow_types names that 86 files import via orchestrator.workflow (deterministic_runner.py and digest.py among them), loading the 18k-line module just for the WorkflowOutcome enum.
findings.proposal: Move _select_train_members (and its _line_ranges_stackable helper) into the lane and have workflow import it downward. Move StaleEvidenceRejection, the exception the lane catches, to a module both layers can import downward (task_status or shared). Make compute_preexisting_main_break_fingerprint a lane- or verify-level function. Then convert workflow's deferred lane imports to module-level imports of the façade. Structural: it changes module ownership across workflow/scheduler/lane.

findings.statement: The reclaim timer covers one of the seven producers it is the sole consumer for. That is INV-7 (holds-owned-and-bounded): quarantine parkings are an unbounded hold. `orchestrator/git_ops.py::GitOps.quarantine_worktree` parks into `<worktree_base>-orphaned` for every project an orchestrator runs (7 units). The only reclaimer, reclaim-orphaned-worktrees.service → .sh, hard-codes `REPO=/home/leo/src/dark-factory`. Measured read-only today: /home/leo/src/solar-challenge/.worktrees-orphaned holds 4 parkings, 1.3G, the oldest stamped 20260531T140823Z (about 4 months), and solar-challenge-platform holds 2 (587M). The dark-factory root is empty. The parking age is a meaningful string (heuristic 12): `quarantine_worktree` writes `strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')` into the directory basename, and `scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py::parse_parking_dir_name` re-parses it with its own regex and format constant. Nothing ties the two (heuristic 11; the tests synthesise names). The script is 'always-exit-0', and an unparseable name is skipped with a log line only (INV-11), so drift in either half would leave every parking un-reclaimed while the timer reports success.
findings.proposal: Run the reclaim per project root, for example a templated unit per orchestrator config or iterating the fleet's configured worktree bases. Share the parking-name format from one home, or stamp a parked_at sidecar. Surface a non-zero 'skipped_unparseable' count in the exit status or an escalation.

findings.statement: The briefing's standing deferred-task invariant (a task never sits in `deferred` without a concrete flip-to-pending condition) is stated as a rule with teeth but enforced at no point — heuristic 10 asks for one mechanism, checked at more than one point. Measured read-only against the live task store at review time: 336 tasks are `deferred`; 3 carry a structured condition (`x_deferral` / `deferred_watch`: 2217, 4681, 5531); 23 have only non-done dependency edges or external_deps (dependency-shaped — should be `pending` with edges); 49 mention flip/revisit wording only in prose (unverified); 261 carry no condition by that heuristic. The briefing's own text ('Both current deferred tasks (1147, 1853)') is stale: 1147 is done and 1853 cancelled. The deferral-flip-condition PRD (`plans/deferral-flip-condition-prd.md`) owns the enforcement: 6524 in-progress, 6525–6529 pending (server gate at the status choke point, sweep, census, migration).
findings.proposal: Land the 6524–6529 chain; its census (6528) is what this check should consume next run. No new work beyond that chain.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 and INV-5: a confusion candidate's identity across the census and the codebook merger is its free-text LLM-written title. codebook.apply_coding_record groups candidates by `c.get('title') == title`; census._novel_clusters re-implements that grouping ('mirrors its own title-keyed grouping, codebook.py:494': skip titleless, first-occurrence-wins) so verification spends one call per title; and census._find_pending_candidate_id resolves each verify verdict back to a candidate id by title equality plus `disposition == 'pending'` string comparison. Any divergence - a miner re-wording a title, whitespace, two causes sharing a title - silently drops or misroutes a paid verdict; the pipeline grew DroppedVerdict, CensusOutcome.dropped_verdicts/unresolved_verdicts and a report section to surface those drops after the fact, and the codebook holds the evidence of the class (rejected cand-20260722-28 reappearing as pending cand-20260724-2, cited in both modules). Candidate ids are themselves minted by counting existing ids with the date prefix.
findings.proposal: Mint the candidate id at merge time and carry it through verification (verify the merged candidates, not pre-merge raw records), so verdicts resolve by id; keep title only as display text. Changes the census/codebook contract - structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 4 and 6: run_census is 765 lines (cognitive 81) taking 26 parameters, opening with a 160-line docstring that narrates the whole pipeline (preflight gate, mining, a second headroom gate, verify, synthesis, matrix, merge, promote/reject/retire, validate, filing gate, payloads/submit, record+report write, codebook dump, state advance, commit, ledger) - the purpose is not statable without 'and', and the docstring is the reader's only map. The data crossing its seams is untyped (heuristic 12): verify_fn returns a dict read as `verify_result.get('verified') or []`, `get('headroom_probes')` with an isinstance guard, a mutable `probe_count = [1]` cell; and its result CensusOutcome carries `status: str` ('deferred' | 'done' | 'unlanded') and `deferred_stage: str` ('preflight' | 'verify') with fields whose docstrings say they are 'Meaningful ONLY when status == "deferred"' or set 'iff status == "unlanded"' - a sum type flattened into one product whose validity rules live in prose. Field docstrings defend decisions with task ids (4144) and reviewer-finding numbers (Comments stance).
findings.proposal: Make CensusOutcome a tagged union (Deferred / Landed / Unlanded dataclasses) and verify_fn's result a frozen dataclass; split run_census into stage functions passing typed stage results (mine -> verify -> adjudicate/merge -> file -> persist/commit), with the narration moved to the PRD it summarises.

findings.statement: INV-11 no-silent-fail-soft (partial enumeration): extract_done_count, the sole place a get_statuses payload becomes the census done-count (used by compute_tasks_landed for trigger condition (b) and by census.run_census to persist last_census_done_count), validates the envelope's shape but never looks at the `pagination` key. fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py::get_statuses documents that a response carrying `pagination` is one page (has_more) and that absence means complete, records that auto-pagination was briefly the DEFAULT and regressed exactly these callers, and names 'the standalone status fetcher in scripts/legibility/census_trigger.py' as a consumer that 'reads the map as a complete done-count census' and 'can see no pagination marker'. Today default_status_fetcher sends only {project_root}, so the server returns the full map - completeness rests entirely on the server's default staying put. If it changes again, a first page of at most 2,000 statuses is counted as the whole project and persisted as a baseline, the same fabricated-baseline class task 3291 closed for the error envelope.
findings.proposal: In extract_done_count, raise StatusFetchUnavailable when `pagination` is present with has_more true (or page to completion in default_status_fetcher keyed on has_more), with a test feeding a paged payload.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement, cli_invoke.py (4,459 lines). Prose first (Comments stance): 57.1% of lines are docstring (1,283) or comment (1,265); much is reviewer-answering measurement and rejected-alternative prose (the ~88-line cross-account resume measurement inside invoke_with_cap_retry, the task-3925 INVARIANT block, _materialize_stdin's pipe-capacity alternative), whose home is a commit message or the plan already cited. Partition of top-level symbols, with the h13 symptom each part would hit: P1 outcome shape (AgentResult, is_zero_output_timeout, is_timed_out_with_progress, is_server_error_status, is_cli_invocation_rejected and helpers, require_non_blank_prompt) - AST shows no references to other cli_invoke symbols; needs invocation_outcome.CLI_INPUT_REQUIRED_MARKERS, so if the markers stay put P1 -> invocation_outcome -> P1 is a cycle (invocation_outcome.py line 39 top-imports is_server_error_status, is_zero_output_timeout); moving the markers down with it: none. P2 transcript reader (_resolve_transcript_path through transcript_evidence_for_session, ~830 lines): references no other cli_invoke symbol: none. P3 failure classification (AgentFailureKind/Class, classify_agent_failure, classify_cap_kill, build_failure_message): references only P1 plus invocation_outcome.classify_invocation, all downward: none. P4 spawn and run (build_claude_argv, apply_spawn_env, _invoke_claude, _parse_claude_output, _cpu_* prefixes, _materialize_stdin, _run_subprocess, invoke_claude_agent): imports P1/P2 downward: none. P5 cap retry (invoke_with_cap_retry, _reset_for_fresh_retry, AllAccountsCappedException, resume prompts): imports P4 and usage_gate.scope_for; usage_gate top-imports cli_invoke.AgentResult (P1 after the split), so P5 can import usage_gate at module top: none. Today the single file instead stitches these units with five function-local cycle-breaking imports (invocation_outcome at the CLI-input-marker helpers, in classify_agent_failure and inside the retry loop; usage_gate.scope_for inside invoke_with_cap_retry) - the two cycles cli_invoke<->invocation_outcome and cli_invoke<->usage_gate. Every candidate part passes heuristic 13, so a split is legitimate.
findings.proposal: Split along P1..P5 (P1 below invocation_outcome, P5 above usage_gate), which removes both import cycles and their five deferred imports; move measurement prose to commit messages/plans in the same change. Do the SHL-7 test migration first or alongside, because 23 'shared.cli_invoke.asyncio' and 19 count_transcript_turns patch targets pin current module paths.

findings.statement: INV-2 structured-facts-at-failure, and heuristic 1: _run_subprocess has four distinct kill arms - startup wedge (no turn within startup_grace_secs, default 120 s), working-regime idle bound, working-regime absolute cap, and the flat timeout_seconds ceiling - and logs which one fired, but each raises a bare TimeoutError into one shared kill block, and the returned _SubprocessResult carries only `timed_out=True` (its fields are stdout, stderr, returncode, duration_ms, timed_out, proc_tree, transcript_turns, ended_awaiting_background, model_id). The kill block then writes stderr as 'Process terminated after {timeout_seconds}s timeout (SIGTERM)' / 'Process killed after {timeout_seconds}s timeout', which is false for three of the four arms: a startup-wedge kill at 120 s under a 1800 s ceiling reports '1800s timeout', and an absolute-cap kill (elapsed >= absolute_cap_secs > timeout_seconds) reports the smaller ceiling. Downstream consumers (is_zero_output_timeout, is_timed_out_with_progress, classify_agent_failure) must re-derive the cause from transcript_turns and the stderr text instead of reading the fact the emitter held.
findings.proposal: Carry a `kill_reason` enum (STARTUP_WEDGE / IDLE / ABSOLUTE_CAP / CEILING) and the bound that tripped on _SubprocessResult and AgentResult, raised as a typed internal exception rather than bare TimeoutError; render stderr from it.

findings.statement: Tests stance: shared.cli_invoke is reached by test patch targets by dotted path - invoke_claude_agent (76), terminate_process_group (23), the `asyncio` module binding (23), count_transcript_turns (19), _WATCHDOG_POLL_SECS (14), _run_subprocess (9), _WATCHDOG_WORKING_POLL_SECS (6), VllmBridge (6), read_transcript_records (5), plus _reset_for_fresh_retry, _WATCHDOG_MIN_POLL_SECS, open, datetime, build_claude_argv. The patching now dictates production shape: _run_subprocess's INVARIANT block forbids hoisting a functools.partial because it 'silently defeats every patch('shared.cli_invoke.count_transcript_turns', ...)', and the watchdog's kill routing is described in terms of 'Existing tests that mock communicate(side_effect=TimeoutError)'. The default suite never runs a real subprocess through this path (test_cli_invoke_integration is `-m integration`, deselected), and test_failover_integration.py patches invoke_claude_agent 28 times, so the failover loop is tested above a mocked CLI. A real-subprocess fake CLI already exists - scripts/tests/conftest.py::fake_claude_cli (scripted plans, proven first on PATH) - but shared/tests does not use it.
findings.proposal: Promote fake_claude_cli into a shared test fixture and drive invoke_claude_agent / invoke_with_cap_retry end to end through it (cap banner, 401, 5xx, startup wedge, resume), with the watchdog timings injected as parameters rather than patched module constants; then retire the dotted-path patches.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 (clear invariants, enforced): the briefing's key scenario says LLM-gate budgets must clear the fixed cli_invoke cost floor (~$0.10+), but the floor has no home and no enforcement point. invoke_claude_agent/build_claude_argv pass any max_budget_usd straight to `--max-budget-usd`; the only statements of the floor are comments in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/config/schema.py ('Do NOT lower below 0.25 - the adjudicator becomes a silent no-op'; 'max_budget_usd must comfortably exceed that floor or every call returns error_max_budget_usd before any verdict (silent no-op)'), on fields declared `Field(default=2.00)` with no lower bound - while the adjacent max_turns field does carry `ge=3` for its analogous floor. The floor has already eroded once (0.30 -> 2.00 after cost-per-call rose, per the same comment), so a config edit or a new gate can reintroduce the silent no-op with nothing going red.
findings.proposal: Give the floor one home in shared (a named constant beside build_claude_argv, or a validated budget type) and enforce it at the config models (`ge=`) and at invoke time (refuse or warn with the value). Choosing the floor's owner is a design choice - structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 5, minimum data lifetimes: the loop-local `unattributed_cap` flag in invoke_with_cap_retry is set once (heuristic zero-cost-exit branch, when `slot.lease` is None or `usage_gate.lease_is_current(slot.lease)` is False) and never reset, yet it guards every later `slot.confirm(result.cost_usd)` in the loop (ModelNotFound, CLI-reject retry, ServerError, progress-timeout and the final success arm) and the final `capped_reason = CapReason.ACCOUNT if unattributed_cap else ceiling_reason`. The unattributed branch does not `continue`, so when the attempt was a resume it falls into the 'Non-cap-hit failure while resuming -> fall back to fresh' arm, which does `continue`. Every subsequent attempt - including a fully successful fresh one - then skips slot.confirm, so UsageGate.on_agent_complete never adds its cost to `_cumulative_cost` (the value before_invoke compares against `session_budget_usd` to raise SessionBudgetExhausted), confirm_account_ok never runs for that account (InvokeSlot's __aexit__ only releases the probe slot), and the cost_store row for the RETURNED successful run is written with capped=True, capped_reason=ACCOUNT. A stale lease is an ordinary condition under concurrency (a sibling's transition on the same account bumps `generation`), and with an empty pool (before_invoke returns None) every heuristic cap is unattributed.
findings.proposal: Scope the flag to the attempt: compute `attempt_unattributed` inside the loop body and carry only the RETURNED attempt's verdict to the cost row; settle the slot on every arm through one `settle(result)` helper so a skipped confirm is impossible. Add a test driving heuristic-unattributed -> resume-fallback -> success and asserting cumulative_cost and the stored capped flag.

findings.statement: INV-11, on the 'one account pool from config/usage-accounts.yaml' scenario: UsageCapConfig._load_accounts_file, when accounts_file is set but missing, logs a WARNING 'using inline accounts' and returns; with no inline accounts, UsageGate._init_accounts then falls back (fallback_to_default_credential defaults True) to the operator's ~/.claude login as a single 'default' account. A missing or mis-pathed pool file therefore turns multi-account failover into a one-account fleet with only log lines to say so - the caller cannot tell it from success. The pool path itself has four homes with two different overrides (heuristic 11): dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml `${USAGE_ACCOUNTS_FILE:/home/leo/...}`, orchestrator/defaults.yaml and fused-memory/config/config.yaml `${DARK_FACTORY_ROOT:/home/leo/src/dark-factory}/config/usage-accounts.yaml`, and fused-memory/config/schema.py::_default_curator_usage_cap reading USAGE_ACCOUNTS_FILE with a hard-coded absolute default - so the two processes read the same pool only while both env vars are unset or agree.
findings.proposal: Refuse at load when an explicitly configured accounts_file does not exist (or carry a degraded flag the gate exposes and the orchestrator escalates on); resolve the pool path through one helper and one env var.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12 and 11: TaskStatus (a StrEnum) and the derived TERMINAL/ACTIVE/WORKFLOW_PRESERVE/STATUS_TRIGGERS sets are the declared single vocabulary, and orchestrator/task_status.py now re-exports them, but consumers still route on bare string literals: a regex count finds 176 `status ==/!=/in (` comparisons against a task-status spelling in orchestrator/src, fused-memory/src, escalation/src and dashboard/src (an upper bound - it includes some merge-step/escalation vocabularies sharing spellings and eval-corpus diffs; genuine task-status examples: harness.py `current != 'merge-deferred'`, scheduler.py `ext_status != 'done'`), versus 36 non-test files that import shared.task_statuses at all. fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/flag_dedup.py still declares its own `TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset({'cancelled', 'done'})`. The home's own docstring has drifted (Comments stance): it says the module 'does NOT rewire the call sites above', lists four legacy copies that no longer exist as copies, and its MIGRATION HAZARD note pins task_filter.py 'lines 365, 463, and 625'. scripts/legibility compares 'done' literally in census_trigger.extract_done_count while importing nothing from the vocabulary.
findings.proposal: Migrate consumers to TaskStatus members (a ruff banned-literal or AST ratchet can make the remaining count only fall), delete flag_dedup's copy, and cut the task_statuses docstring to what the module is. Spans packages, hence structural.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: the policy for spawning the Claude CLI (binary resolution, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY strip, env_overrides merge, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, spawn identity) is hand-assembled at three sites: cli_invoke._invoke_claude, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/invoke.py::_invoke_claude_with_sandbox (whose comment says it 'Mirrors shared.cli_invoke._invoke_claude'; only apply_spawn_env and build_claude_argv are shared), and UsageGate._run_probe, which builds its own argv with a hard-coded `'claude'` and its own env. The probe therefore ignores claude_binary_spec()/resolve_claude_binary(), whose CLAUDE_BINARY override is the documented remediation for the 2026-08-13->18 unresolvable-PATH incident and is what fused-memory's curator_escalator.py and task_curator.py tell operators to set. On a host that follows that advice instead of pinning PATH, agent invocations work but every cap-resume and auth re-probe raises ProbeSpawnError: _reprobe_account returns leaving the account AUTH_FAILED until an operator SIGHUP, and _account_resume_probe_loop keeps backing off, so CAPPED accounts re-open only through the reset-clock sweep. Latent today: every installed unit pins Environment=PATH.
findings.proposal: One spawn-env builder in shared (strip, overrides, token, config dir, spawn identity) used by all three sites, and the probe argv built through claude_binary_spec()/build_claude_argv. Spans shared and orchestrator, hence structural; the probe's binary alone is a one-line fix.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: one cap is recorded as `account_events.event_type='cap_hit'` by two writers with different semantics. UsageGate._transition fires a 'cap_hit' cost event (details = JSON {reason, resets_at}) on each entry to CAPPED, and _handle_cap_detected's scoped branch fires its own; independently, invoke_with_cap_retry calls `cost_store.save_account_event(event_type='cap_hit', details=label)` on every exact cap detection, including a sibling's detection on an already-CAPPED account (which takes no transition). The heuristic-net path writes only the gate row. The orchestrator wires both writers to the same store (harness.py sets usage_gate._cost_store and passes cost_store to every invoke_with_cap_retry). Measured read-only on the live data/orchestrator/runs.db: since 2026-09-01 there are 215 cap_hit rows (131 JSON-reason gate rows, 84 label rows) against 102 'resumed' rows, e.g. max-e at 2026-10-07T16:10:10.106255 (label 'Escalation watcher (auto)') and .106465 (gate JSON) for one event. dashboard/data/costs.py counts `event_type = 'cap_hit'` rows as cap events and dashboard/data/cap_history.py pairs cap_hit/resumed FIFO, so duplicates inflate counts and leave unpaired cap_hits rendered as open-ended cap intervals.
findings.proposal: Pick one owner of the 'cap_hit' fact: the gate's transition (per-account state change) is the natural home; record the per-invocation observation under a distinct event type (e.g. 'cap_observed') or drop it. Decide whether dashboards want transitions or observations - a design choice, hence structural.

findings.statement: WEAKENED known gap. The briefing says the LOAD_SAMPLES_SCHEMA copy of sampler.store._SCHEMA has 'no automated sync check' (tracking null); in the tree it has one: dashboard/tests/test_load_data.py::test_load_schema_and_metrics_match_sampler asserts byte equality with sampler.store._SCHEMA and compares the names collect_psi/collect_process_metrics actually emit with PSI_METRICS/PROCESS_METRICS (ran it: passes). What remains: (1) it is still lockstep duplication (inv-5 prefers extraction) and production never executes LOAD_SAMPLES_SCHEMA — the dashboard ships a constant only its tests use; (2) the guard reaches a private name (sampler.store._SCHEMA) and is `pytest.importorskip`, so an environment without the sampler package turns it into a skip; (3) the metric vocabulary is spelled independently in sampler.metrics (f-string emission), sampler.sampler (_PSI_METRICS/_PROCESS_METRICS/_LOAD_METRICS/_LOAD_STEMS validation), dashboard load.py, and scripts/load-threshold-calibration.py, and per-cgroup identity is encoded inside the metric string (`own_cpu_some10:<leaf>`, split on ':' by sampler.sampler::_matches_a_stem) rather than a column (heuristic 12).
findings.proposal: Put the schema and the metric-name vocabulary (exact names, stems) in `shared` (both packages depend on it) and import from both sides; drop the copy and the private-name test. Optionally a leaf column instead of the ':' suffix. Structural (spans packages).

findings.statement: _build_eval is ~295 lines with ten parameters, four of which are output accumulators the function mutates in place (issues, consumed, linked_fingerprints, storm_suppressed — heuristic 8, mutating shared structures rather than returning values; heuristic 5 by extension, since their lifetime spans every eval of the build). It loads and validates the run series, unions metric ids, reads limits, computes staleness, validates kinds across the window, joins verdicts, joins escalations with storm suppression, and shapes each row (heuristic 4). Cognitive complexity 64, the slice's maximum. Many inline comments defend micro-decisions to a reviewer (e.g. why a dedup key is deliberately NOT routed through _short_repr) rather than explaining the code. The module's never-raise/issues-list contract itself is sound (inv-11 compliant).
findings.proposal: Return a small result value (rows, issues, consumed keys, linked/suppressed fingerprints) per eval and merge in build_memory_evals; extract the per-metric kind validation and the escalation join into their own functions. Structural only in that it changes internal signatures; could be mechanical.

findings.statement: The chunked whole-tree walk is a production path with no production caller: fetch_tasks' own docstring says 'no production caller passes chunk_size today', and git grep confirms the only callers are app._fanout_probe_completion and task_snapshot (neither passes chunk_size); 21 test call sites keep it alive. It costs _walk_pages (147 lines, the module's cognitive maximum at 22), the _CompleteRead mode of the _TasksRead record, and roughly half of fetch_tasks' ~110-line docstring (chunk-vs-page naming, five coherence checks). Heuristic 9: interface surface without functionality behind it in production; tests stance: tests pinning a path production does not take.
findings.proposal: Delete the chunk_size parameter, _CompleteRead's chunk field and _walk_pages with their tests (git history keeps them if the transport limit returns). Mechanical.

findings.statement: Under the Tests stance, the private patch targets locate a missing seam. `watcher.main` (116 lines) does five jobs in one body: argv parsing, logging setup, the baseline snapshot, inotify arming, the initial scan and the event loop with deadline arithmetic (heuristic 4). It takes no injectable inotify source, clock or emitter. So escalation/tests/test_watcher.py drives it by patching module internals: `escalation.watcher._initial_scan` (12 patches), `escalation.watcher._send_ntfy` (1), and module globals `escalation.watcher.INotify` (17), `.sys` (23), `.time` (5) and `.urllib` (6). These tests pin the call structure of main, not watcher behaviour, and a refactor that keeps the behaviour will still break them.
findings.proposal: Extract a pure `watch(source, clock, scan, emit, *, deadline, excludes)` that main wires to INotify/time/stdout. Drive it in tests with a fake event source and a real tmp queue dir. Mechanical, but it changes the test surface.

findings.statement: Comments stance: _construct_llm_client is 143 lines of which 82 are comment lines (57%), most defending decisions to a reviewer — 'must not be "simplified" away' (twice), 'This is a DELIBERATE behaviour change (task 3864)', 'No preflight on this arm — deliberately' — and pinning line numbers inside the vendored graphiti library (openai_base_client.py:51-67, client.py:80, :176,187, :191-192), which drift on the next upgrade. The file overall is 0.54 prose with 56 task-number references. The executable logic (~58 lines: provider × client_class selection) is straightforward once the prose is removed.

findings.statement: Heuristic 1: TaskmasterConfig's docstring says 'Only project_root and tool_mode are read by SqliteTaskBackend', but no source outside schema.py reads tool_mode (git grep over fused-memory/src finds none; config.yaml still sets tool_mode: "all"), and http_url and OpenAIProviderConfig.organization_id are likewise defined and never read. findings.statement: Dead code: `_task_metadata_spawned_from` has no caller or test anywhere in the tree (`git grep -w` finds only its definition); it dates from the curator's first landing (8d265e32a8, 2026-04-11).

findings.statement: Heuristic 13 reach-back symptom, judged weak: agent_loop.py, cli_stage_runner.py and judge.py (plus 3 test modules) import _RECONCILIATION_STAGE_CAP_WAIT_SANITY_SECS (1800.0) from the 6-line package __init__, which imports nothing, so no cycle can form. findings.statement: INV-11: any fetch exception (and a missing taskmaster or non-absolute root) returns an empty FilteredTaskTree(), which has no completeness field, so Stage 1/2/3 and remediation cannot tell 'fetch failed' from 'no active tasks'; the only detector is indirect (cross_verify_task_counts flags total_mismatch if the separate get_statuses census succeeded; if both fail it returns available=False, consistent=True). Against the key decision 'recon must not load the full task tree on the event loop', every full cycle issues an unfiltered get_tasks for the whole project and runs the pure-Python filter_task_tree on the loop thread. Weakened: per-cycle (not per-transition) and the large blocking sites are allowlisted with owners.
findings.proposal: Carry a fetch status on FilteredTaskTree rendered into stage payloads; fetch only active statuses or offload the filter.

findings.statement: The only live comment marker in scope, `TODO(task σ / session-resume)`, guards an invariant in prose instead of code (heuristic 10; Comments stance): the run-config-dir GC in `_recover_one_run` is unconditional and is safe only because `disposition` is always 'failed' today; the marker says a future resumable disposition MUST gate the GC or the transcript --resume depends on is destroyed. 'task σ' is not a task id, the session-resume series 2771–2777 is done, and no open task's brief covers this gate, so it is also untracked under the briefing's TODO-tracking convention.
findings.proposal: Encode the invariant: skip `gc_run_config_dir` when the disposition is resumable (or assert the disposition is non-resumable), with a test, and delete the marker. One anchor, no design choice.

findings.statement: Heuristic 3: the per-project axis of reconciliation behaviour has two mechanisms. ReconciliationConfig already keys per-project values by project_id in config (backlog_hard_limit_overrides: dict[str, int]), but snapshot-write exemption and contamination-ceiling retirement are Python source modules naming four project ids (policies/autopilot_video.py, know_live.py, dark_factory.py, solar_challenge_platform.py) folded into SNAPSHOT_WRITE_BLOCKED_PROJECTS / CONTAMINATION_CEILING_RETIRED_PROJECTS, consumed at 23 sites (harness, flag_dedup, prompts/stage3, task_knowledge_sync ...). Onboarding or changing a project's posture is therefore a fused-memory code change and merge, not a config edit beside the project's other knobs. Heuristic 1: the docstring's 'Note on the shared name' concedes membership means two different things (server-side write rejection vs census not in use) under one predicate.
findings.proposal: Move both registries into ReconciliationConfig as per-project fields (or a per-project policy map), keeping the predicates; split the two meanings of 'snapshot write blocked' if callers ever need the reason. Structural (config contract).

findings.statement: INV-5 / heuristic 1: per-stage tool denial has one source table (cli_stage_runner.py STAGE1_/STAGE2_/STAGE3_DISALLOWED; the StructuredOutput carve-out correctly lives once in shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py::_SCHEMA_OUTPUT_TOOL), but the stage prompts restate the same capabilities as hand-passed literals: stage1.py passes can_file_tasks=False 3× and can_escalate=False 1×, stage2.py can_file_tasks=True 3× and can_escalate=True 1×, stage3.py can_escalate=False. One prompt statement is false: stage2.py tells the agent subtask creation is 'blocked via DISALLOW_SUBTASK_CREATE', a name defined nowhere in src. The reviewed stage-safe half of the policy (_REVIEWED_STAGE_SAFE) lives only in tests/test_stages.py — a policy fact homed in a test file.
findings.proposal: Derive can_file_tasks/can_escalate from STAGE*_DISALLOWED (e.g. whether mcp__fused-memory__submit_task is denied); delete the phantom DISALLOW_SUBTASK_CREATE reference; move the stage-safe set into src beside the denylists.

findings.statement: INV-4, residual of codebook one-shot-subagent-contract (22 sightings), which is otherwise remediated in the present tree: CodebaseVerifier.verify now returns structured agent_failed + failure_token (codebase_root_unresolved, cli_output_empty, api_refusal ...), recorded as a verify|codebase|agent_failed run_action row; Judge.review_run routes transport failures to _handle_infra_failure with a per-project streak and truthful halt. But nothing aggregates verifier failures: no reader of those rows or of verification_agent_failed exists in dashboard/, scripts/, fused-memory/scripts or server/, and verify.py's own comments note a project whose root lacks .git 'would refuse that project's every sparse verification forever'. The judge's sibling path has a streak gate; the verifier's does not. (Codebook unverified-task-premises' 'premise_lint unconsumed' claim is REFUTED: middleware/premise_lint_guard.py::premise_lint_error calls it and server/tools.py runs it in submit_task for recon-stage-* callers.)

findings.statement: Heuristic 13: services/__init__.py eagerly re-exports MemoryService and PlannedEpisodeRegistry, but zero modules in fused-memory src or tests import either name via the package path (`from fused_memory.services import MemoryService|PlannedEpisodeRegistry` → 0 hits; 24 other `from fused_memory.services import` lines import submodules). Its only effect is that importing ANY services submodule (topic_anchor, durable_queue, ...) loads the 11,323-line memory_service — the edge middleware/dead_letter_escalator.py::_error_class blames for its cycle-breaking function-local import, and part of the cycle topic_anchor cites to justify a duplicated constant (FMR-26). A re-export kept with no consumer plus a deferred import it forces.
findings.proposal: Empty services/__init__.py of imports; hoist dead_letter_escalator's deferred import (or delete it via FMR-6).

findings.statement: INV-2: DurableWriteQueue._handle_failure composes error = f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}' (optionally prefixed with POST_EXECUTE_DEAD_PREFIX) and DeadLetterEvent carries only that string plus a structured post_execute flag (whose comment says 'Structured, so the consumer never re-parses POST_EXECUTE_DEAD_PREFIX'), yet middleware/dead_letter_escalator.py::_error_class strips that prefix and splits on ': ' to recover the exception class name the emitter had as type(exc).__name__ — an ad-hoc parser of an internal value (h12). Importing the prefix forces a function-local import whose own docstring says it breaks the cycle dead_letter_escalator → services/__init__ → memory_service → dead_letter_escalator (h13).
findings.proposal: Add error_class (and raw message) fields to DeadLetterEvent, populated in _handle_failure; delete _error_class's parsing and the deferred import.

findings.statement: Dead code: `run_tournament` is marked deprecated in its own docstring (use `run_elo_tournament`) and `git grep -w` finds no caller or test anywhere in the tree; it has been unchanged since it landed in d3b14de810 (2026-03-19). findings.statement: INV-5 no-lockstep-duplication, plus heuristic 9 layering. The escalation-watcher wire contract (header names X-Escalation-Levels and X-Escalation-Identity, and identity 'orchestrator-escalation-watcher-auto') has its canonical home in a PRIVATE constant of the upper-layer harness.py. escalation/src/escalation/authority.py::_WATCHER_AUTO_IDENTITY duplicates it by hand ('Must equal orchestrator.harness._WATCHER_ESCALATION_HEADERS[...]; duplicated (not imported) to preserve the escalation -> orchestrator layer direction'). escalation/server.py separately defines _LEVELS_HEADER and _IDENTITY_HEADER. Tests import orchestrator.harness._WATCHER_ESCALATION_HEADERS across the layer boundary to pin the copies. The duplication exists only because the definition sits in the wrong layer: harness.py already imports escalation.* at top level and could import the constants from escalation. Comments stance: harness.py's 'CONTRACT' comment still says 'No test in this repo exercises this constant against the live server parser', which is false since escalation/tests/test_capability_guard_http.py::TestWatcherConstantLockstep (whose docstring cites closing exactly that gap).
findings.proposal: Define the header names and watcher identity once in escalation (for example in escalation.authority) and have harness.py import them. Drop the cross-layer test pin and the stale comment. The change spans two packages but involves no design choice.

findings.statement: LaneLifecycle.read returns None for both 'no record' and 'record present but unparseable', logging only a WARNING, and all_records silently drops corrupt records (inv-11: the caller cannot tell fewer from all). The class already has _read_or_raise to make that distinction, but the readers never get it. harness.py::Harness._recover_crashed_tasks reads 'rec = self.git_ops._lane_lifecycle.read(entry)' and treats None as 'no record at all — the pre-W11 compat case', which falls through to the heuristic adopt/cleanup path. So a corrupt record for a QUARANTINED lane is handled like a never-recorded lane, the 'adopt-on-doubt' the surrounding comment says must never happen. Writes are atomic (tmp + os.replace), so this is rare. Every consumer reaches the store through another module's private attribute, git_ops._lane_lifecycle: harness.py, stranded_verified_green.py and task_runtime.py (h7).
findings.proposal: Return a tri-state (record / absent / corrupt) or raise CorruptLaneRecord from the public read. Have all_records report what it skipped. Expose the lifecycle from GitOps through a public accessor or pass it explicitly to its readers.

findings.statement: Dead code: `_resolve_commit_tree` is referenced nowhere but its own definition and log string, yet its docstring instructs callers that 'use this to gate a skip-verify decision' to treat None as fail-closed — a contract with no callers in the merge lane's 22,081-line main module, where a reader looking for the skip-verify gate will be misled.
