findings.statement: 'Coalesce' names two different mechanisms in the same file and façade (h1). coalesce_or_enqueue_merge_request, the merge_coalesced event, registry.record_coalesced and MergeDispatchResult(in_flight=True) mean MCP-path de-duplication of a second submission for the same branch. train_coalesced, the 'coalesce-' train ids, _maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles, _coalesce_derailed_task_ids and merge_train_coalesce_enabled mean forming an atomic train from different branches. The briefing's key scenario uses 'COALESCED' in the second sense, and the façade exports the first under the public name coalesce_or_enqueue_merge_request (imported by escalation/server.py). An agent asked to change coalescing can land in the wrong mechanism.
findings.proposal: Rename the de-dup gate and its event to a de-dup vocabulary (for example dedupe_or_enqueue_merge_request / merge_deduplicated), keeping the old event name only if a wire consumer needs it. This touches the façade and escalation server, so it is a contract change.

findings.statement: Heuristic 13 symptoms: OfflineLaneWorker reaches its collaborators through function-local imports — `from orchestrator.verify import _extract_failing_test_ids, _serial_pytest_str` (two private names) and two imports of helpers from orchestrator.workflow (compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint, build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments), an upward reach into the per-task workflow layer for functions that exist only for the offline lane. The docstring justifies the verify import as avoiding 'an offline_lane <-> verify import cycle', but verify does not import offline_lane (importing orchestrator.verify leaves orchestrator.offline_lane, orchestrator.workflow and orchestrator.git_ops out of sys.modules), so the stated cycle does not exist — a comment that misleads the next agent about the module graph.
findings.proposal: Move the two offline-lane helpers out of workflow.py into offline_lane.py (or a shared lower module), import public verify helpers at module top, and delete the false cycle note. One anchor, no design choice.

findings.statement: Possibly dead — verify before removing: `rebase_cost_readout` (readout helpers for the task-1802 rebase-distance → verify-cost telemetry) is imported only by orchestrator/tests/test_rebase_verify_cost.py; no src module, CLI command, script, unit or skill invokes it, and hold_history.py mentions it only in a comment. If the readout is run by hand it has no documented entry point.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12: set_task_status decides retry-vs-raise by is_transient_rejection, a substring search for 'TimeoutError', 'ConnectionError', 'ReadTimeout'... over the string extract_rejection built by concatenating the payload's error and hint (or, for success=False, the whole payload repr) — although the same envelope is parsed a second time by extract_structured_rejection, which exposes the structured error/error_type fields (two parsers of one envelope, heuristic 11). A business rejection whose hint or payload text mentions a timeout is retried as transient. Statuses are plain str throughout the scheduler (status: str parameter; 15 string-literal status comparisons such as == 'merge-deferred' / == 'done') although shared.task_statuses.TaskStatus is a StrEnum, so a misspelt literal type-checks.
findings.proposal: Parse the envelope once into a typed rejection (error_code, error_type, hint), classify transience on error_type, and type statuses as TaskStatus. One anchor, no design choice.

findings.statement: Heuristic 13 symptom (re-export shim kept so an old path resolves): orchestrator/src/orchestrator/usage_gate.py still exists as `from shared.usage_gate import *` plus an explicit tuple (AccountState, ProbeSpawnError, SessionBudgetExhausted, UsageGate). Five production imports in the orchestrator package go through it (harness.py, review_checkpoint.py, steward.py, workflow.py twice) while evals/runner.py, evals/reviewer_trial/runner.py and workflow_types.py import shared.usage_gate directly - two spellings for one name in one package. The shim is a lockstep site, not drift-free: a star import only reaches shared.usage_gate.__all__, which deliberately omits public names (AccountLease per its comment; PoolFrozen too), and two tests exist only to keep it honest - orchestrator/tests/test_usage_gate.py::TestReExportShimParity (identity of ProbeSpawnError through the shim) and an AST scan of the shim file in shared/tests/test_auth_failed.py.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 / INV-5: the task-priority vocabulary ('critical','high','medium','low','polish') and its ordering are declared four times across three packages with no shared home — orchestrator/config.py::PRIORITY_TIERS (+PRIORITY_RANK, DEFAULT_TIER), fused-memory server/tools.py::_PRIORITY_TIERS, fused-memory middleware/task_curator.py::_PRIORITY_RANK (+DEFAULT_PRIORITY), and dashboard app.py::_VALID_BOOST_TIERS — and the findings contract's completion weights restate it a fifth time. Adding or renaming a tier is a four-file lockstep edit whose misses validate silently (a tier unknown to the curator ranks as KeyError or default; to the dashboard, as a 400).
findings.proposal: Define the tier enum once in shared (alongside task_statuses) and import it in all four places. One vocabulary, no design choice beyond its home.

findings.statement: The review briefing's dashboard and sampler sections state facts the tree has outgrown (inv-9 one-fact-one-home: the briefing restates world-facts with no reconciliation). (1) dashboard known_gap 'scheduler view shows only ACTIVE-TOP parks ... tracking 1868' — landed: scheduler.py passes snapshot park_stacks through, _stranded_park_rows emits rows for dead owners, and app.py serves /api/v2/dashboard/scheduler/evict-park. (2) sampler known_gap 'no automated sync check' for the load schema — test_load_schema_and_metrics_match_sampler exists (DASH-15). (3) sampler purpose/scenarios say 9 metrics and a 24-hour window 'per-tick prune + daily VACUUM'; store.py now retains 30 days, prunes at most once per 24h, VACUUMs only above a 10% free-page fraction, and writes 11 + 2 per cgroup leaf metrics (25 on the measured host). (4) dashboard purpose says 'Read-only monitoring web UI' while app.py proxies six write tools (cancel_ticket, set/clear_task_priority_override, reorder_pin_queue, request_park_eviction). Every /review seat is steered by these statements.

findings.statement: The sampler's prose (store.py 58%, metrics.py 44%, sampler.py 54%) is dominated by reviewer-answering material the Comments stance assigns to the commit message: cleanup_old's docstring is mostly a measured rejected alternative (CREATE INDEX idx_samples_ts, 98->130 MB, 106.7 ms no-op scan), write_tick's docstring carries two benchmark tables, run_tick carries a 20-line defence of keeping write-only window columns, and metrics.py's collect_load_metrics carries a 25-line defence of a log level. Files do not make sense in isolation (heuristic 13): metrics.py uses PRD-decomposition letters as names for modules and tasks — 'α's read_runqueue_ratio', 'it is α's file, out of this task's scope', 'β's recorded G7 waiver', 'ε1/ε2 calibrate' (14 occurrences) — that resolve only through plans/load-throttle-harmonisation-prd.md. Dated state claims will drift (inv-9): 'measured on this host on 2026-09-13 there are ZERO df-*.slice (task 3394 has not landed)', '25 in total on this host today'.
findings.proposal: Move measurements and rejected alternatives to the commit log or the PRD with a one-line pointer; replace Greek task letters with module names (shared.psi); drop dated host-state claims. Mechanical (prose rehome, no behaviour change).

findings.statement: Heuristic 13: the legibility modules import their siblings under two names. census.py does `import codebook`, `import coder`, `import filing_policy`, `import config` (bare, resolved via scripts/legibility on sys.path) alongside `from legibility import census_trigger, ...`; coder.py does `import codebook as codebook_mod` while nightly.py and census_trigger.py import `legibility.codebook`. In one process these load twice: importing legibility.nightly with the test path layout leaves both sys.modules['codebook'] and sys.modules['legibility.codebook'], distinct objects whose NeverDeleteError classes are not the same type (checked: `a.NeverDeleteError is b.NeverDeleteError` is False), so an `except codebook.NeverDeleteError` written against one spelling misses the other's raise. Each file also carries its own copy of the __main__ sys.path bootstrap and the _SHARED_SRC insertion ('Mirrors census.py/nightly.py's identical guard'), an INV-5 lockstep across census.py, coder.py, nightly.py, sampling.py, account_pool.py and check_transcript_persistence.py.
findings.proposal: Use the `legibility.` package spelling everywhere and one bootstrap entry point (a tiny runner or `python -m legibility.<tool>`), deleting the per-file sys.path blocks.

findings.statement: Heuristic 1 (a description that says one thing while the code does another): the module docstring states the gate 'is fed from the invocation choke point via ApiHealthGate.report and read by the scheduler (dispatch throttle), the workflow (steward suppression), the harness (watcher-rotation deferral) and the escalation lifecycle', but no src module imports `shared.api_health` at the pinned tree — only shared/tests/test_api_health.py does, and usage_gate.py / cost_store.py mention it in comments. The core landed under task 3325 (done, 2026-07-31); the wiring is task 3327, still pending two months later. An agent reading the docstring will believe dispatch is already throttled on provider degradation.
findings.proposal: Until 3327 lands, say in the docstring that the consumers are planned (pointer to 3327 / plans/server-side-api-error-handling-prd.md C4). One anchor, no design choice.

findings.statement: Answer to the briefing question: async_sqlite_base.apply_full_durability_pragmas is the de-facto home for aiosqlite stores and they use it (ticket_store, event_buffer, sqlite_task_backend's write connection, server/tools.py stores, AsyncSqliteBase.open; side read connections use apply_wal_pragmas only, and scheduler_state's aiosqlite.connect is a read-only URI), and the sync stores use sqlite_sync_base.apply_full_durability_pragmas_sync. But the triad's VALUES have no single home (INV-5): `wal_autocheckpoint=100` and `journal_size_limit=67108864` are literal in both async_sqlite_base.py and sqlite_sync_base.py, and fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/event_journal.py::EventJournal._apply_pragmas re-declares them as _JOURNAL_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT/_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES 'Kept in sync with that helper' instead of calling apply_full_durability_pragmas_sync. In the same module two methods named checkpoint() have opposite contracts for one condition (INV-11, heuristic 10): AtomicConnection.checkpoint returns the sentinel CheckpointResult(-1, -1, -1) when the pragma yields no row, AsyncSqliteBase.checkpoint raises RuntimeError; both docstrings warn that a store moving between them changes behaviour 'with no type or test signal' and name task 5562 as the unifier.
findings.proposal: Define the triad once as named constants (or a frozen pragma spec) consumed by both helpers; make event_journal call apply_full_durability_pragmas_sync. Unify checkpoint() on the raising contract under task 5562.

findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement, usage_gate.py (3,052 lines). Prose first: 49.9% (885 docstring + 638 comment lines). Partition and h13 symptom per part: U1 vocabulary/types (AccountPhase, IllegalTransitionError, ProbeSpawnError, _LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, ScopeCap, AccountState, AccountLease, SessionBudgetExhausted, PoolFrozen, scope_for): leaf, none. U2 InvokeSlot: its report()/detect_cap_hit() call UsageGate private members (_handle_cap_detected, _handle_auth_failure, _handle_near_cap_warning, _fire_cost_event) through self._gate, so in its own module it would reach into another module's private names - an h13/h7 symptom unless those handlers become a public reporting interface. U3 probe machinery (_sweep_stale_probe_dirs_once, _load_probe_result, _probe_* helpers, UsageGate._run_probe 202 lines, _account_resume_probe_loop 112, _reprobe_account, spawn-fault accounting ~140): mutates accounts through self._transition and reads self._accounts, so a satellite would be a function-bag over the gate's private state - the cheat heuristic 14 names; legitimate only as a Prober returning a verdict value the gate applies. U4 scope-cap overlay (8 _scope_* methods): reads self._accounts/self._config - same satellite symptom. Separately, usage_gate.py line 57 imports the private `_parse_resets_at` from invocation_outcome. So only U1 splits cleanly today; the 2,315-line UsageGate class owns account selection/leasing, the phase machine, probing and the scope overlay (heuristic 6), which is why its parts cannot be separated without first narrowing their interfaces.
findings.proposal: Record this measurement; if the gate is reworked (SHL-6), extract a Prober that returns OK/Capped/SpawnFault verdicts and make InvokeSlot's reporting calls public gate methods, after which U2-U4 split legitimately.
